slides.text:
The AI Control Towerfor business reinvention
Luca Morlupi
Sr. Manager, Solution Consulting
Moad
Author: Luca Morlupi
Today we’ll talk about how ServiceNow is not just a technology platform—it is the AI platform for business transformation.Our goal is clear: to eliminate complexity, reduce manual work, and allow people and processes to focus on what truly creates value.Why does this matter to you? Because every organization today must do more with less. With AI embedded in ServiceNow, you can:
Cut operational costs by automating repetitive work and removing inefficiencies.
Boost productivity by accelerating decisions and execution.
Enhance customer and employee experience through faster, more personalized interactions.
Ensure trust and scalability with governance and security built in.
And this isn’t about a distant future—these capabilities are already available and ready to use today.Let me now show you how today’s conversation will be structured: a clear and simple path to connect the dots.
Italiano:Oggi parliamo di come ServiceNow non sia solo una piattaforma tecnologica, ma la piattaforma AI per la trasformazione del business.Il nostro obiettivo è chiaro: eliminare la complessità, ridurre le attività manuali e consentire a persone e processi di concentrarsi su ciò che genera davvero valore.Perché è importante per voi? Perché ogni organizzazione oggi deve fare di più con meno. L’AI integrata in ServiceNow vi consente di:
Ridurre i costi operativi automatizzando attività ripetitive ed eliminando inefficienze.
Aumentare la produttività accelerando decisioni ed esecuzione.
Migliorare l’esperienza di clienti e dipendenti con interazioni più veloci e personalizzate.
Garantire fiducia e scalabilità, grazie a governance e sicurezza integrate.
Non parliamo di un futuro lontano, ma di capacità già disponibili e pronte all’uso.Ora vi mostro come sarà strutturata la conversazione di oggi: un percorso chiaro e semplice che ci aiuterà a collegare i punti.

Author: Luca Morlupi
Let me start by sharing a few numbers that can help frame who ServiceNow is.We are a company with over 28,000 employees in 33 countries, growing steadily at about 20% year over year. We work with more than 2,800 global partners, which allows us to be close to many customers across different markets.In the past year alone, we released over 6,000 new features, reflecting our ongoing commitment to innovation and to keeping the platform up to date.One metric we are particularly proud of is our 97% renewal rate: nearly all of our customers continue to work with us year after year. For us, that is a strong signal of trust and perceived value.When we say “The world works with ServiceNow,” we mean that our platform is used in very diverse contexts: from banks to governments, from manufacturing companies to telecom providers.We don’t see ourselves just as an IT platform, but as an enterprise platform that helps connect people, processes, and data, creating a simpler, more consistent experience.
Italiano:Vorrei iniziare condividendo qualche numero che ci aiuta a inquadrare chi è ServiceNow.Siamo un’azienda con oltre 28.000 persone in 33 paesi e stiamo crescendo a un ritmo costante, intorno al 20% anno su anno. Collaboriamo con più di 2.800 partner globali e questo ci permette di essere vicini a tanti clienti in mercati diversi.Solo nell’ultimo anno abbiamo rilasciato più di 6.000 nuove funzionalità, un segnale del nostro impegno costante a innovare e a mantenere la piattaforma aggiornata.Un dato a cui teniamo molto è il 97% di renewal rate: significa che quasi tutti i nostri clienti scelgono di continuare a lavorare con noi anno dopo anno. Per noi è soprattutto un segnale di fiducia e di valore riconosciuto.Quando diciamo che “il mondo lavora con ServiceNow”, intendiamo che la nostra piattaforma è utilizzata in contesti molto diversi: dalle banche ai governi, dalle aziende manifatturiere alle telco. L’85% delle aziende Fortune 500 hanno scelto la piattaforma ServiceNow.Non ci consideriamo solo una piattaforma IT, ma una piattaforma enterprise che aiuta a connettere persone, processi e dati, offrendo un’esperienza più semplice e coerente.

On the previous slide, we saw how ServiceNow has continuously expanded and strengthened its core platform, with AI innovation accelerating in recent years.Here we can zoom in on the automation journey itself.We started with Phase 1: scripted workflows and integrations, designed to digitize manual, repetitive tasks—bringing structure and standardization.Then came Phase 2: predictive workflows, powered by machine learning and models that learn from data to anticipate needs and improve efficiency.Phase 3 introduced conversational AI, enabling more natural, human-like interactions for employees and customers, making work simpler and more intuitive.And today we are in Phase 4: agentic workflows and AI Agents. These are no longer just executing tasks—they can reason, plan, and make decisions, adapting in real time to support the organization.On the next slide, we’ll see how this Agentic AI experience comes to life, bringing automation even closer to the way people actually work.
Italiano
Nella slide precedente abbiamo visto come ServiceNow abbia costantemente ampliato e rafforzato il proprio core, con un’accelerazione importante grazie all’innovazione AI negli ultimi anni.Ora entriamo più nel dettaglio del percorso dell’automazione.Siamo partiti con la Fase 1: workflow scriptati e integrazioni, pensati per digitalizzare attività manuali e ripetitive, portando ordine e standardizzazione.Con la Fase 2: workflow predittivi, grazie al machine learning, i sistemi hanno iniziato ad apprendere dai dati, anticipando i bisogni e migliorando l’efficienza.La Fase 3 ha introdotto la conversational AI, che ha reso le interazioni con la piattaforma più naturali e immediate, sia per gli utenti che per i dipendenti.Oggi siamo entrati nella Fase 4: agentic workflows e AI Agents. Non si tratta più solo di eseguire attività, ma di sistemi che sanno ragionare, pianificare e prendere decisioni in tempo reale, adattandosi alle esigenze dell’organizzazione.Nella prossima slide vedremo come questa nuova fase prende vita concreta con l’esperienza Agentic AI, rendendo l’automazione ancora più vicina al modo in cui le persone lavorano.

After looking at the evolution of automation, now we move into the concrete: AI Agents.This slide shows how ServiceNow isn’t just talking about artificial intelligence – it’s already recognized by analysts as a leader in building and managing AI Agents.The key point here is that this isn’t about a distant future – it’s available today. ServiceNow’s AI Agents are not isolated bots, but intelligent agents embedded in your business processes, powered by the unified data model and orchestrated by the platform’s workflows.This means they can handle requests, classify and assign tasks, interact with external data, and most importantly, collaborate with each other like a real digital team.The value is twofold: on one side, they eliminate a large amount of manual work, freeing up time for higher-value activities; on the other, they create new seamless experiences for both employees and customers.It’s like having a digital team of assistants, always available, working for you 24/7.In the following sections, we’ll look at practical examples and real-world use cases that show how these AI Agents are already being applied today to accelerate transformation.

We are uniquely positioned to differentiateand capture theAI opportunity
Hyperscalers deliver infrastructure and building blocks. We are the enterprise-wide system of action, as the workflow automation leader with relevant business context. Across any data, any model, any cloud.
Data platforms are where data is stored, curated and used to train AI. ServiceNow is where AI is actioned and applied to run the enterprise, accessing any data or model.
LLMs lack enterprise controls, business context, or native governance. We offer enterprise-grade AI with enterprise-scale business context, trust and ecosystem. We combine probabilistic with deterministic flows. Offer choice across models.
SoRs trap work in silos. Only ServiceNow orchestrates cross functional workflows and delivers E2E fulfillment across the enterprise on a single platform.
Foundation Model Platforms
Hyperscalers
Data platforms
Systems of Record
When we talk about the AI landscape, there are four main layers — and ServiceNow plays a unique role that connects them all.
At the top, we have the hyperscalers like AWS and Google. They provide the infrastructure and computing power — the foundation for AI — but they don’t operate at the workflow or business process level.
Then we have data platforms such as Palantir, Databricks, and Snowflake. These are where data is stored, curated, and used to train AI models. But AI only creates value when it’s put into action — and that’s exactly where ServiceNow comes in. We are where AI is applied operationally to run the enterprise.
Below that are foundation model platforms like Anthropic and OpenAI. They provide the intelligence — but they often lack enterprise-grade control, governance, and context. ServiceNow brings this context, governance, and trust layer, enabling organizations to use AI responsibly and effectively across processes.
Finally, we have systems of record — SAP, Salesforce, Workday — where data lives, but often in silos. Only ServiceNow orchestrates workflows across these systems, delivering true end-to-end execution on a single, unified platform.
This combination — connecting infrastructure, data, intelligence, and systems of record — is what uniquely positions ServiceNow to capture the AI opportunity across the enterprise.
Italiano
Nel panorama dell’intelligenza artificiale possiamo distinguere quattro livelli principali, e ServiceNow ha un ruolo unico nel connetterli tutti.
In alto troviamo gli hyperscaler, come AWS e Google, che forniscono l’infrastruttura e la potenza di calcolo necessarie all’AI, ma non operano sui processi o sui workflow aziendali.
Poi ci sono le piattaforme dati come Palantir, Databricks e Snowflake, dove i dati vengono archiviati, gestiti e usati per addestrare i modelli di AI. Tuttavia, l’intelligenza artificiale genera valore solo quando viene applicata ai processi operativi — ed è qui che entra in gioco ServiceNow, la piattaforma dove l’AI diventa azione concreta.
Al livello successivo troviamo i foundation model, come Anthropic e OpenAI. Offrono intelligenza, ma spesso mancano di controllo, governance e contesto aziendale. ServiceNow aggiunge proprio questi elementi, fornendo AI di livello enterprise, sicura e governata.
Infine, ci sono i system of record — come SAP, Salesforce e Workday — che contengono i dati ma restano spesso isolati. Solo ServiceNow orchestra i workflow tra questi sistemi, garantendo un’esecuzione end-to-end su un’unica piattaforma.
È questa capacità di collegare infrastruttura, dati, intelligenza e sistemi operativi che rende ServiceNow unica nel catturare l’opportunità dell’AI a livello enterprise.

Author: Luca Morlupi
This slide clearly illustrates something we see all the time: when a customer asks for help, things often get complicated.Not because people don’t want to help, but because behind the scenes there are too many teams, too many tools, and too many handoffs.Each function — from IT to HR, from customer service to back office — uses different apps, systems, and processes.The result? Information gets lost, data lives in silos, and what should be a simple request turns into a painful journey.Today, companies use on average more than 367 applications. So it's no surprise that processes break down, activities require manual effort, and the overall experience — both for the customer and for internal teams — becomes frustrating.The key message here is simple:If your organization doesn’t operate in a coordinated way,if you don’t have a single platform connecting people, data, and workflows,it becomes very hard to deliver fast, effective, and seamless service.So earlier we saw how difficult it can be for customers to get the support they need.Here, we’re looking inside the organization — and things aren’t much better for employees.Even a simple internal request — like getting access, ordering a device, or updating personal data — triggers a complex chain: multiple departments, disconnected systems, approval workflows, manual steps… and all of this often leads to delays, mistakes, and frustration.But the most critical issue?Those who should have visibility and control — HR, IT, Procurement, Compliance — are chasing scattered data.There’s no single view to understand where the process gets stuck, how long things take, or what to improve.So not only is the employee experience poor, but also the people who want to improve how the organization works are left without the insights they need.And this is exactly where an integrated platform becomes essential: to orchestrate the entire process, provide end-to-end visibility, and enable continuous improvement.
Italiano
Questa slide racconta bene una cosa che vediamo spesso: quando un cliente chiede assistenza, si innesca un percorso complicato. Non perché le persone non vogliano aiutare, ma perché dietro ci sono tanti team, tanti strumenti, tanti passaggi.
Ogni funzione – dall’IT all’HR, dal customer service al back office – usa applicazioni diverse, sistemi diversi, processi diversi. E il risultato? Le informazioni si perdono, i dati non parlano tra loro, e alla fine rispondere a una richiesta semplice può diventare un incubo.
Le aziende oggi usano in media più di 367 applicazioni. È facile capire perché i processi si spezzano, le attività si fanno a mano, e l’esperienza – sia per chi chiede supporto, sia per chi lavora dentro – diventa frustrante.
Quello che vogliamo far passare è questo: se non si lavora in modo coordinato, se non si ha una piattaforma che unisce persone, dati e processi, diventa davvero difficile offrire un servizio efficace e veloce.
Quindi, se prima abbiamo visto quanto sia complicato per i clienti ricevere supporto, qui vediamo che anche per i dipendenti le cose non vanno molto meglio.
Anche una semplice richiesta interna – un accesso, un dispositivo, un cambio dati – attiva un processo che coinvolge più dipartimenti, sistemi diversi, approvazioni, passaggi manuali... e spesso tutto questo si traduce in attese, errori e frustrazione.
E la cosa più critica è che chi dovrebbe avere visibilità e fare governance del processo – HR, IT, Procurement o chi si occupa di compliance – si ritrova a rincorrere i dati. Non c'è un punto unico da cui capire dove si inceppano i flussi, quanto tempo si perde, o come ottimizzare.
Quindi non solo l’esperienza per il dipendente è negativa, ma anche chi vuole migliorare l’organizzazione è bloccato dalla mancanza di visibilità e controllo.
Ed è proprio qui che entra in gioco il valore di una piattaforma integrata: orchestrare tutto questo, dare visibilità end-to-end e abilitare il miglioramento continuo.

Author: Luca Morlupi
Each department—Customer Service, IT, HR, Back Office—runs its own stack of tools, databases, and user interfaces.
Now AI has been added, but as Sidecar AI: disconnected, bolt-on assistants sitting on top of tools.
They don’t connect to workflows or systems of action. They generate content, but they don’t move work forward.
Users are forced into context switching between portals and AI tools, ending up with shallow insights and inconsistent experiences.
This creates the point solution trap: many mini-AI tools that don’t scale, each with its own license, interface, and governance problem.
The impact: fragmented data, inefficiency, higher costs, and greater risks around Security, Compliance, Responsible AI, Governance, and Cost Control.
Ultimately, it’s lipstick on a broken experience. What’s needed is a single AI connected to clean data, unified workflows, and enterprise systems of action.
Italiano
Ogni dipartimento - Customer Service, IT, HR, Back Office—usa i propri strumenti, database e interfacce.
Oggi si è aggiunta l’AI, ma come Sidecar AI: assistenti scollegati, appiccicati agli strumenti esistenti.
Non sono collegate ai workflow o ai sistemi di azione: generano contenuti, ma non fanno avanzare davvero il lavoro.
Gli utenti devono continuamente fare context switching tra portali e AI scollegate, ottenendo solo insight superficiali ed esperienze incoerenti.
È la trappola delle point solution: tante mini-AI che non scalano, ciascuna con la propria licenza, interfaccia e problemi di governance.
Le conseguenze: dati frammentati, inefficienza, costi crescenti e rischi su Sicurezza, Compliance, Responsible AI, Governance e Controllo dei Costi.In definitiva, è solo “rossetto” su un’esperienza rotta. La soluzione è un’unica AI connessa ai dati puliti, ai workflow unificati e ai sistemi di azione enterprise.Author: Luca Morlupi

Author: Luca Morlupi
This is one of the most important slides, as it shows how a digital transformation can be built step by step using the ServiceNow platform. Each point on this map represents a capability that can be progressively activated, but at the core is a unified data model that powers the organization’s Digital Portfolio.[Click 1 – Employee Services & ITSM]It all starts with people. First with employee services – HR, knowledge, workplace – then IT, with requests, incidents, and changes. Here, AI plays a crucial role: reducing noise, automating repetitive tasks, and speeding up responses.[Click 2 – Operations Management + Service Operations]This is where ITSM and IT Operations, traditionally separate, converge to form Service Operations. Structured workflows like incidents, requests, and changes combine with operational visibility – discovery, service mapping, anomaly detection, AIOps.The synergy brings tangible results: an alert can automatically trigger a pre-filled incident, routed to the right team. Less manual work, fewer errors, faster resolution. With AI Agents, we go further: predicting and preventing issues. The goal: zero incidents, zero outages.[Click 3 – CSM + FSM]Once operations are under control, we extend externally, to customers. With Customer Service Management, agents have real-time visibility of orders, assets, and services, and can collaborate directly with IT, supported by generative AI.When field work is needed, Field Service Management ensures the right technician, at the right time, with the right tools – all on mobile. A seamless flow between front-line and back-end.[Click 4 – Asset Management]Another pillar is asset management, for both hardware and software. ServiceNow manages the entire lifecycle, integrated with the CMDB.For hardware: automated inventory, tracking, and assignments.For software: visibility, compliance, and license optimization.The value: lower costs, simplified audits, reduced risk.[Click 5–9 – Strategic Portfolio Management]Now we move to strategy. Ideas and business demands enter structured pipelines. With ServiceNow, we define the roadmap, align it with OKRs, and fund it transparently.Approved initiatives become projects managed via Agile, Waterfall, or hybrid methods. PMOs and project managers work on one platform with full visibility into timelines, resources, and outcomes.In parallel, Enterprise Architecture rationalizes applications, manages technology risk, and ensures alignment, all tracked in the Common Service Data Model.[Click 10 – Sourcing & Procurement]Procurement, often overlooked, has major impact. ServiceNow digitizes it end-to-end: from request to contract to receipt. Every step tracked, every order visible.[Click 11 – Risk Management]Resilience is built on risk. ServiceNow embeds Risk Management into daily operations: risks are identified and assessed in real time, tied to services, assets, vendors. Policies and controls are digitized, aligned to regulations such as DORA, NIS2, ESG.[Click 12 – Security Operations]Next comes security. With ServiceNow, SecOps are integrated into business operations. Vulnerabilities are prioritized by business impact, alerts resolved via automated workflows, and threat intelligence accelerates response, reducing residual risk.[Click 13 – Sales & Order Management]Finally, the commercial lifecycle: from lead to quote, order, fulfillment, and post-sale service. Sales, procurement, and operations all connected, keeping the customer at the center.ConclusionWhat ties everything together is the ServiceNow AI Platform: one unified data model, integrated workflows, and distributed intelligence. Each new step builds on the previous, delivering visibility, automation, and value from day one.
Italiano:Questa è una delle slide più importanti, perché ci mostra come sia possibile costruire una trasformazione digitale passo dopo passo, sfruttando la piattaforma ServiceNow. Ogni punto che vedete in questa mappa rappresenta una capability che può essere attivata in modo graduale, ma il vero cuore che tiene tutto insieme è il modello dati unificato, che alimenta il Digital Portfolio dell’intera organizzazione.[Click 1 – Employee Services e ITSM]Tutto inizia dalle persone. Prima i servizi per i dipendenti – HR, knowledge, workplace – poi quelli IT, con la gestione delle richieste, degli incident e dei cambiamenti. Qui l’AI gioca un ruolo chiave: riduce il rumore operativo, automatizza attività ripetitive e rende più veloce la risposta.[Click 2 – Operations Management + Service Operations]Qui vediamo l’incontro tra ITSM e IT Operations, due mondi che storicamente lavoravano in parallelo. Insieme creano le Service Operations: da un lato i flussi strutturati (incident, request, change), dall’altro la visibilità operativa (discovery, service mapping, anomaly detection, AIOps).La sinergia porta risultati concreti: un alert può generare automaticamente un incident già compilato, con tutte le informazioni necessarie e assegnato al team giusto. Meno errori, meno lavoro manuale, più velocità. Con gli AI Agents, il sistema non solo reagisce, ma anticipa e previene. L’obiettivo è chiaro: zero incident, zero outage.[Click 3 – Customer Service Management + Field Service Management]Una volta messe in sicurezza le operations, ci si apre verso l’esterno, verso i clienti. Con il Customer Service Management offriamo un’assistenza realmente connessa: gli agenti vedono lo stato degli ordini e dei servizi e possono collaborare in tempo reale con l’IT, supportati dall’AI generativa.Quando serve un intervento sul campo, entra in gioco il Field Service Management: il tecnico giusto, nel momento giusto, con tutte le informazioni già sul dispositivo mobile. Un flusso continuo tra front-line e back-end, senza interruzioni.[Click 4 – Asset Management]Un altro pilastro è la gestione degli asset, sia hardware che software. Con ServiceNow possiamo seguire l’intero ciclo di vita: dall’acquisto alla dismissione, integrato con la CMDB.Per l’hardware: inventario automatizzato, tracciamento fisico, assegnazioni.Per il software: visibilità sulle installazioni, compliance e ottimizzazione delle licenze.Il valore? Riduzione dei costi, audit più semplici, meno rischi.[Click 5–9 – Strategic Portfolio Management]Qui ci spostiamo sul livello strategico. Si parte da idee e iniziative, che vengono valutate e inserite in pipeline dinamiche. Con ServiceNow possiamo definire la roadmap, collegarla agli obiettivi (OKR) e finanziarla in modo trasparente.Le iniziative approvate diventano progetti gestiti con metodologie Agile, Waterfall o ibride. PMO e Project Manager lavorano su un’unica piattaforma, con piena visibilità su tempi, risorse e risultati.Accanto alla delivery c’è l’Enterprise Architecture: razionalizzazione applicativa, gestione dei rischi tecnologici e pianificazione coerente. Tutto tracciato nel Common Service Data Model.[Click 10 – Sourcing & Procurement]La gestione degli acquisti ha un impatto enorme. Con ServiceNow digitalizziamo il processo end-to-end: dalla richiesta al contratto, fino alla ricezione. Ogni passaggio è tracciato e trasparente.[Click 11 – Risk Management]La resilienza si costruisce gestendo il rischio. ServiceNow integra il Risk Management nei processi operativi: rischi rilevati e valutati in tempo reale, collegati a servizi, asset e fornitori. Policy e controlli digitalizzati e sempre verificabili, anche per normative come DORA, NIS2, ESG.[Click 12 – Security Operations]Accanto al rischio, c’è la sicurezza. Le SecOps con ServiceNow non sono a sé stanti, ma parte del flusso. Vulnerabilità e alert vengono prioritizzati in base all’impatto, con workflow automatizzati e threat intelligence integrata. Risultato: risposta rapida e riduzione del rischio residuo.[Click 13 – Sales & Order Management]Infine, la parte commerciale: dalla lead generation al preventivo, dall’ordine alla consegna, fino al supporto post-vendita. Tutto connesso, dal procurement alle operations, mantenendo il cliente sempre al centro.ConclusioneQuello che tiene insieme tutti questi step è la AI Platform di ServiceNow: un unico modello dati, workflow integrati e intelligenza distribuita. Ogni nuovo passo rafforza il precedente, portando visibilità, automazione e valore fin dal primo giorno.
Contributors: Sara Gaviano, Roberto Dossi, Giuseppe Picarella

Author: Luca Morlupi
This slide highlights the real value of what we call Autonomous IT, powered by AI Agents. It’s not just about automating repetitive tasks – it’s about radically transforming how IT operates, boosting productivity while cutting costs.Let’s look at the numbers:
Around a 75% reduction in Tier 1 tickets. Most common and repetitive requests are handled autonomously by the platform, with no need for manual intervention.
A 70–90% reduction in mean time to resolution (MTTR). Problems are identified, triaged, and resolved much faster – often before a user even opens a ticket.
A 40–50% decrease in hardware, software, and cloud spend. Thanks to improved visibility and automated optimization, waste is eliminated, compliance is strengthened, and costs go down.
A 50% increase in projects delivered on time. With less effort spent on firefighting, IT teams can focus on innovation and execute strategic initiatives more effectively.
The key message for you is clear: with Autonomous IT, IT shifts from being a cost center constantly chasing issues, to becoming a proactive enabler that dramatically reduces manual effort and accelerates digital transformation.
Transition: In the next section, we’ll see how these outcomes are not just theoretical but already a reality for many organizations that have adopted ServiceNow’s AI-powered platform.
Italiano:Questa slide mette in evidenza il vero valore di quello che chiamiamo Autonomous IT, reso possibile dagli AI Agents. Non si tratta solo di automatizzare attività ripetitive, ma di trasformare radicalmente il modo in cui l’IT funziona, migliorando la produttività e riducendo i costi.Guardiamo i numeri:
Una riduzione di circa il 75% dei ticket di primo livello. Questo significa che gran parte delle richieste più semplici e frequenti viene gestita in autonomia dalla piattaforma, senza bisogno di coinvolgere manualmente un operatore.
Una riduzione del 70-90% dei tempi medi di risoluzione (MTTR). Qui l’impatto è enorme: i problemi vengono identificati, triaggiati e risolti molto più velocemente, spesso senza che l’utente debba nemmeno aprire un ticket.
Una riduzione del 40-50% della spesa per hardware, software e cloud. Grazie a visibilità e ottimizzazione automatizzata, si evitano sprechi, si migliora la compliance e si liberano risorse economiche.
Un aumento del 50% nei progetti completati on time. Con meno effort dedicato alla gestione quotidiana, i team IT possono concentrarsi sull’innovazione e portare avanti iniziative strategiche con più efficacia.Il messaggio chiave per voi è semplice: con l’Autonomous IT l’IT non è più un centro di costo che rincorre i problemi, ma diventa un abilitatore proattivo, capace di ridurre drasticamente il lavoro manuale e accelerare la trasformazione digitale.Passaggio: Nella prossima sezione vedremo come questi risultati non sono teorici, ma sono già realtà per molte aziende che hanno adottato la piattaforma ServiceNow con AI Agents.

Speaker Notes
•
When IT Service Management and IT Operations Management use the same data model - IT Service Management change processes are tightly integrated into IT Operations.
And this allows – Operations teams to easily see the service impact of a planned change before approving it. Since roughly 80% of IT incidents are associated with “change” - being able to see the service impact of an issue before approving a planned change is critical to keeping digital services running.
And when service and operations are consolidated on the same platform- IT Service Management data also provides historical: incident, problem and change information to the IT operations team –which significantly reduces the time it takes to remediate problems – slow services and outages -
For instance, by finding similar previous incidents when a service outage occurs, clients can accelerate service restoration by identifying the potential root cause in near real-time and they will also have information to see how the issue was remediated in the past.
1.Unauthorized Change: In general Change is the cause of roughly 80% of the incidents or issues in IT. Unauthorized changes are the worst kinds of change because they happen often and they are usually a result of an unauthorized change from someone in IT: either IT Operations, or SecOps, or a DevOps team member. When an unauthorized change happens that results in an outage or an unresponsive service for example and when Service and Operations are separate tools it can take hours to investigate and remediate the cause – to determine the outage or the slow service was in fact the result of an unauthorized change.
When Service and Operations are on the same ServiceNow Platform and an unauthorized change happens: As part of the ServiceNow Service Mapping integration with ServiceNow ITSM, the Change Management application that is part of ITSM - receives an event notification – from ITOM - that an unauthorized change activity has been detected . As a result, an emergency unauthorized change request is created for the relevant CI (affected infrastructure or app). And in near-real time the Operations team can review and approve or reject the unauthorized change from the Change Management application – and also importantly revert the change back again in near real-time. So instead of taking hours to investigate and remediate the issue the time to repair is significantly reduced.
●
2. Major Incidents: When Service and Operations are separate tools when it comes to major incidents – for example if SAP crashes; It takes a long time for IT Operations teams to first determine if an actual major incident or outage occurred – because they have to dig through hundreds of events and determine what is an actual issue verses a false positive and it take just as long to resolve it – leaving employees frustrated and unable to access the impacted services.
•When ITSM and ITOM are on the ServiceNow platform: the thousands of events coming into ServiceNow Event Management (ITOM AIOps) from the various monitoring tools across the customers enterprise - get converted to alerts and incidents; When the Alert becomes an incident – it automatically shows up in the Agent Workspace (ITSM) as an Incident or major incident;
•For every major incident that is created in ITOM - a major Incident is proposed in ITSM where the Major Incident Management process kicks off an automated workflow that sends Major Incident notifications to: on-call teams, automatically creates outage records, and updates the employee portal to advise employees of the major outage – e.g. The SAP service has been interrupted
•With IT Service Management and IT Operations Management working together on the same platform this significantly reduces MTTR and employee frustration - employees will know in real time because the employee portal is updated - what services are impacted, that there is in fact an outage and that it is being remediated.
3. Single Data Model:
Often, people confuse tools and business functions. For example, they equate ITSM with the service team or what use to be called the service desk. Similarly, ITOM capabilities such as discovery and event management are seen as tools for IT operations.
•For example, IT operations needs to resolve high-priority incidents. In fact, event management and incident management are intimately connected. The same goes for changes—high-quality IT operations depends on robust change processes, and change history is critical when trying to diagnose service outages.
•Similarly, the IT service teams needs an accurate, up-to-date view of IT services and infrastructure. This is critical for everything from resolving user issues to managing hardware and software assets. And, where does this information come from? It’s held in the CMDB, it ultimately comes from discovery and service mapping—which is an ITOM function.
•So, when ITSM and ITOM are separate tools, IT becomes slow and unresponsive. For example, think about a service outage or degradation. Event management correlates monitoring data and shows you the service impact – but what then?
•When it’s time to act, IT operations has to raise a corresponding incident and route it to the right internal group or vendor.
•When there are separate systems, this causes significant delays at the worst possible time. And, when it comes to fixing the outage, critical information such as alerts, service topologies, and previous incidents and changes are spread over two systems, making it even harder to quickly restore service.
•Having a single data model for IT Service Management and IT Operations Management changes all of this and significantly reduces the time to remediate an incident, or outage in addition to predicting and preventing before incidents before they impact users or the business.
4. DevOps
When it comes to DevOps, automating change processes by integrating directly to DevOps tooling, reduces the overhead burden on DevOps teams without reducing your ability to track changes and ensures the right levels of control and audit are available to reduce risk. Also by creating a unified real-time view across your CI/CD pipeline and production environment, you directly influence the key metrics that DevOps cares about most, including deployment frequency, change failure rate, mean time to restore, and lead time for changes—improving pipeline performance, increasing service availability, and accelerating innovation.
If needed additional DevOps Examples:
Restoring service faster
Most service outages in a cloud-native environment are due to software or configuration changes. To restore service quickly, DevOps/SRE teams typically
revert to the previous release and then investigate the underlying issue. However, to revert, an SRE needs to correlate failures in the production environment
with recent changes pushed out of the CI/CD pipeline. By automatically connecting pipeline and production data in a unified real-time view, you
simplify this correlation process and accelerate service restoration.
Accelerating service issue diagnosis and remediation
While reverting restores the service, it doesn’t remediate the root cause of the problem—or even identify which software or infrastructure change is
responsible. For example, a change in an upstream service can cause downstream microservices to fail.
To diagnose and fix the problem, you need to understand how microservices interact to deliver a service, mapping both
monitoring data and software changes to this service topology. The topology isn’t readily available in the CI/CD pipeline and needs to be discovered in the
production environment. And, until you have resolved the issue, your CI/CD pipeline is impacted. By creating a unified real-time view across your pipeline
and production environment, you accelerate remediation and reduce deployment delays.
Reducing the risk of software changes
By using operational data to make decisions about your CI/CD pipeline, you manage your value stream and reduce risk. For example, error budgets and
service level objectives (SLOs) are measured in your production environment. Understanding how you are performing against these helps you to make
better decisions about your pipeline. For instance, if a specific DevOps team is consuming a large part of the error budget for a service, you can place the
team under additional controls to avoid further failures. You can also identify trusted teams with low failure rates and relax their controls to accelerate
change delivery.
Driving continuous pipeline performance improvement
By creating a unified view of your CI/CD pipeline and linking this to operational data, you make your pipeline measurable. This allows you to identify bottlenecks
and issues that are negatively impacting pipeline performance. For instance, you can now see how long it takes agile stories to make it into
production and identify which pipeline stages are causing delays. You can use your operational history (for example, resolved outages) to identify gaps
in your testing strategy. And you can also measure and improve your organizational performance by identifying skill gaps that manifest themselves in
your pipeline. In other words, by creating a unified real-time view across your CI/CD pipeline and
production environment, you directly influence the key metrics that DevOps
cares about most, including deployment frequency, change failure rate, mean
time to restore, and lead time for changes—improving pipeline performance,
increasing service availability, and accelerating innovation.
•service graph connectors move data and relationships from existing technology systems onto your ServiceNow platform where they can instantly automate workflow and make better data-driven decisions. Service Graph Connectors quickly and easily pull data from your public cloud (from Amazon Web Service, from Azure and from the Google Cloud Platform). The connectors quickly and easily pull data from your Endpoint management systems like Microsoft’s System’s Configuration Manager) from your security systems (like Extrahop) an from your Network systems.
•ServiceNow discovery also fortifies your discovery with additional best-in-class solutions. We can deploy MID Servers to painlessly transport data and relationships from your enterprise to ServiceNow. We can run agentless, agent-based, cloud native, and even Open Telemetry architecture for collection. Automated mapping of services via Machine learning marries the technical details to their business contexts
Shortly after implementing you’ll find you can already solve deviling problems like certificate management, firewall auditing and exceptions, and dozens of other service and operations use cases.
Those outcomes all rely on the business context that ITOM Visibility provides. This context is invaluable and sets the platform apart from its competitors.

This slide shows how ServiceNow enables workflows to be powered by data, artificial intelligence, and automation. The central idea is that no matter where the data resides, the platform makes it available in real time to orchestrate enterprise processes.Through APIs, we can unify data across multiple systems. With Remote Tables, we can display external data without replication, reducing complexity and risk. Event streaming ensures real-time updates, which is essential for processes that demand speed and responsiveness.On the adaptation side, workflows continuously improve with process mining, which identifies bottlenecks and inefficiencies. New, adaptable workflows can then be built with low-code, increasing the pace of innovation without relying on heavy development.Efficiency grows with rules-based automation, while conversational AI makes interactions more natural and immediate, enabling faster and more intuitive actions.In short, workflows are no longer rigid processes. They are dynamic structures that adapt to change and are fueled by data and AI to generate continuous value.Transition: Having seen how workflows become smarter and more adaptive, we will now look at concrete examples of the technologies that allow us to fully exploit these capabilities.
Italiano:Questa slide ci mostra come ServiceNow consenta di potenziare i workflow collegando dati, intelligenza artificiale e automazione. L’idea centrale è che qualunque sia la fonte dei dati, la piattaforma li rende disponibili in tempo reale per orchestrare i processi aziendali.Grazie alle API, possiamo unificare i dati attraverso sistemi diversi. Con le Remote Tables possiamo visualizzare dati esterni senza doverli replicare, riducendo così complessità e rischi. L’event streaming, inoltre, garantisce aggiornamenti in tempo reale, fondamentale per processi che richiedono velocità e reattività.Sul fronte dell’adattamento, i workflow migliorano continuamente grazie al process mining, che individua colli di bottiglia e inefficienze. Possiamo poi costruire workflow nuovi e adattabili con il low-code, aumentando la velocità di innovazione senza dipendere da sviluppo complesso.Infine, l’efficienza cresce con l’automazione basata su regole, mentre l’introduzione della conversational AI rende le interazioni più naturali e immediate, abilitando azioni veloci e intuitive.In sintesi, i workflow non sono più processi rigidi, ma strutture dinamiche che si adattano ai cambiamenti e si alimentano con dati e AI per generare valore continuo.Passaggio: Dopo aver visto come i workflow diventano più intelligenti e adattivi, vedremo ora esempi concreti di tecnologie che permettono di sfruttare al massimo queste capacità.

Author: Luca Morlupi
This slide brings us to see structured workflows in action within the platform. Here it is important to emphasize how the user experience is consistent and intuitive: teams work in dedicated workspaces where dashboards, records, and automations coexist in a single interface.The goal is not only to execute tasks faster but also to provide an environment that guides people in their daily work. Thanks to the unified data model, all information is already connected, and workflows guide users step by step, reducing errors and speeding up completion times.Another key point to highlight is flexibility: workflows can be easily configured and adapted with low-code tools, allowing organizations to quickly respond to new needs without depending on long development cycles.In this way, ServiceNow transforms the very concept of a workflow: from static sequences of tasks into dynamic, intelligent, and personalized journeys.Transition: In the upcoming slides, we will go into more detail on how workflows, combined with artificial intelligence, can support different corporate departments and specific industries.
Italiano:Questa slide ci porta a vedere i workflow strutturati all’opera, all’interno della piattaforma. Qui è importante sottolineare come l’esperienza utente sia coerente e intuitiva: i team lavorano in workspaces dedicati, dove dashboard, record e automazioni convivono in un’unica interfaccia.L’obiettivo non è solo eseguire attività più velocemente, ma offrire un ambiente che accompagni le persone nel loro lavoro quotidiano. Grazie al modello dati unificato, tutte le informazioni sono già collegate, e i workflow guidano gli utenti passo dopo passo, riducendo errori e accelerando i tempi di completamento.Un altro punto da enfatizzare è la flessibilità: i workflow possono essere configurati e adattati facilmente con strumenti low-code, consentendo alle organizzazioni di rispondere rapidamente a nuove esigenze senza dipendere da lunghi cicli di sviluppo.In questo modo, ServiceNow trasforma il concetto stesso di workflow: da sequenze statiche di attività a percorsi dinamici, intelligenti e personalizzati.Passaggio: Nelle prossime slide entreremo più in dettaglio su come i workflow, combinati con l’intelligenza artificiale, possano supportare diversi reparti aziendali e settori specifici.

We treat Data, Privacy, and Security seriously
Generative AI, or GenAI as it is commonly known, is a powerful new tool that promises a paradigm shift in the way the world works and collaborates.
Now Assist from ServiceNow utilizes GenAI, enabling customers to use domain-specific models to improve productivity and efficiency, deliver better self-service, provide recommended actions, give answers, and make searches more effective.
With such a tool, customers naturally need to understand the implications of using this technology and be satisfied that it meets their security and compliance requirements.
ServiceNow is a founding member of the AI Alliance in partnership with IBM, Meta, and other leading organizations to advance the principles of open, safe, and responsible AI globally.
AI data residency
Customer data is stored within their Now Platform instance and customer data always stays within regional boundaries.
For AI processing ServiceNow operates regional colocation facilities in AMS (Canada), EMEA (Germany), and APJ (Japan) and may employ Azure infrastructure within the region for additional capacity if required.
Data processing
Customer data is processed separately from other customers and customer prompts and responses are purged immediately after processing. They are not stored by ServiceNow.
One customer’s prompts and responses are never made available to any other customer.
Customer controllable
By configuring the Sensitive Data Handling plugin, Personally Identifiable Information (PII) and other sensitive data can be masked, so that it does not appear in generative AI prompts.
Customers can elect to opt-in for data sharing, if they so choose. When a customer has agreed to share their data, ServiceNow collects, cleanses for PII, and stores prompts and response data in a secure AI development environment for model improvements.
Customers can opt-out of data sharing with ServiceNow at any time using the Now Assist admin panel within the instance.

BASIC AI AGENTS DATA FLOW
Trigger goes to AI Agent Orchestrator, can be from the Now Assist Panel, Email, or database trigger.
The AI Agent Orchestrator performs an LLM call to OEM Azure OpenAI GPT or Now LLM to plan the overall workflow – this includes decomposing the use case and identifying sub-task assignments.
One or more AI Agents may be used to resolve the sub-tasks, or the resolution could just be a message back to the user via the Communicator Agent.
The AI Agent Orchestrator assigns subtasks to AI Agents on the agent team, each agent sends its own LLM call to plan its next action using ReAct-style reasoning (thought, action, observation).
The AI Agent will use the tools assigned to it, skills can be assigned as tools. Any skills assigned as a tool will follow their normal architecture and data flow (Now LLM, SN OEM Azure OpenAI, 3rd Party BYO LLM), see the Now Assist OOTB and Custom Skill flows for more information.
If a AI Agent encounters uncertainty or blockage, it escalates to the Orchestrator, which performs another LLM call to OEM Azure OpenAI GPT or Now LLM for Reflection, and perform replanning based on the request from the AI Agent.
If During the ReAct engine loop, if there is more input needed from the user, the Communicator Agent will reach out to the user for more information.
The AI Agents will report back to the AI Agent Orchestrator, ultimately, the Consolidation of all tasks will be done by the AI Agent Orchestrator.
The AI Agent Orchestrator will perform any final reflection, memory logging, and resolution output.

INFORMATION AND LEGEND
This slide speaks to ServiceNow Commercial Cloud customers.
Purple solid is for components within the customer’s instance.
Data at rest is only within the customer’s instance when using GenAI, and it is encrypted, same as any other Now Platform capability.
Data is in Transit when using our compute hubs or OEM endpoints using TLS 1.2 encryption.
Purple dotted are optional and configurable components in the customer’s instance.
Green solid is for Now LLMs, SLMs, and services hosted in ServiceNow Compute Hubs.
Azure AI Service used for Now Assist Dynamic Translation and is hosted in ServiceNow Compute Hubs.
Now Assist Guardian is using a Now SLM, but it has been marked distinctly here for customers to understand it runs in parallel from our Now LLMs/Other LLMs.
Green dotted is SN OEM Azure OpenAI service that uses our Azure vNet to connect to an OEM endpoint: compute, APIs, and accounts are managed by ServiceNow. The models are not fine-tuned.
Light blue solid is the ServiceNow local data center where the customer’s instance is hosted.
Light blue dotted is for eligible and opted-in data-sharing customers - training and development for our Now LLM models is done in a dedicated data center hosted in the US.
Filtered AI Content is housed in a different data center than our inference/processing data centers.
Filtered AI Content is defined as ServiceNow owned content, and not customer owned content.
White dotted is for 3rd party BYOK (Key) models that customers manage and host.
Customers are responsible for the hosting, management, understanding of processing and policies of their third-party LLMs.
DATA FLOWS
1 – User performs work within ServiceNow using Now Assist.
1a – If the action occurs in Virtual Agent or Agent Chat, and the customer has the Sensitive Data Handler installed and configured, PII will be masked in the conversational interface.
2 – If Now Assist Guardian guardrails are turned on, data is sent to a ServiceNow compute hub for processing per the enabled guardrails, i.e. sensitive topic detection.
The current guardrails for are:
Offensiveness detection
Security – detection of prompt injection
Sensitive topic detection (Now Assist HRSD)
3 – Customer-configured ACLs with multi-factor authentication apply.
4 - Along with standard Now Platform data security and domain separation to limit user access to data.
5, 6 - Now Assist feature is triggered, and the request prompt is sent to the Generative AI Controller.
6a – Now Assist Guardian logging is triggered when the prompt is sent to the controller.
7 - If configured, Data Privacy for Now Assist masks configured sensitive data patterns from the prompt before being sent to the LLM.
8a – If configured by the skill Now LLM Service receives the input and generates a response.
8b - In the event that there is high demand: Input delivered to the Now LLM Service hosted in Azure vNET, and a response generated.
8c – If configured by the skill, SN OEM Azure OpenAI service receives input and generates a response.
9 – Now Assist Guardian enabled guardrails check the response prior to delivering the response to the user if blocking is turned on, an error message will be delivered to the user for outputs containing offensive content or prompt injection.
10 - Response returned to customer instance. Data (including the input and output of the response) is deleted from the data center. Response received by the customer instance and displayed for the user. Log of the interaction stored in a hidden log table. No AI-generated content has been stored or written on the record.
11 - Response is edited/accepted by end user, feedback can be logged during this stage. Note: This stage is what determines if AI generated content is written to and stored on the record, i.e. adding summarization to work notes.
12 - If eligible and have not opted out: Data from the log table (prompts, responses, feedback, additional context) is extracted for use in training our LLMs. Data is anonymized and cleansed of PII before leaving the instance and is now Filtered AI Content. Filtered AI Content is received by our training environment and hosted in ServiceNow AI Development data centers.

These hubs support AI inference for the Now LLM Service. During periods of high traffic, workloads may burst to ServiceNow-managed infrastructure in Microsoft Azure using a ServiceNow-controlled private vNet. No data is routed over the public internet.
ServiceNow also operates in-country Compute Hubs in:
United States
United Kingdom
Switzerland
These in-country hubs guarantee national data residency. Azure bursting and OEM models are not supported in UK or Switzerland in-country hubs.
Opt-Out Controls
Customers can manage data routing and usage preferences in the Now Assist Admin Console or AI Control Tower.
Data Sharing for Model Improvement: Controls whether anonymized prompts and responses (Filtered AI Content) are shared with ServiceNow to improve the Now LLM Service.
Overflow Processing (Azure Bursting): Controls whether inference traffic can burst to ServiceNow-managed Azure vNets during high-load scenarios.
Note: Regulated Markets, FedRAMP, MSP, SLED, and non-US-based customers are opted out of data sharing by default.In some environments, opt-out settings may be locked and default to off for compliance or eligibility reasons.
Predictive Intelligence and AI Services
These services are included in the Now Platform’s non-generative ML offering and include:
AI Search
Attachment malware scanning (requires Data Privacy SKU)
Predictive Intelligence for classification, regression, and similarity models
These services do not use generative models or LLMs. Inference occurs entirely within the customer’s ServiceNow instance or the ServiceNow local data center.
Legend – Network and Processing Boundaries
Light Blue Solid Line – ServiceNow Local Data Center
This is the co-location facility where the customer’s Now Platform instance resides.
Also used to support Predictive Intelligence, AI Search, and other traditional ML workloads.
Data processing occurs inside the ServiceNow-controlled environment.
Purple Solid Line – Customer Instance: Core Components
Located entirely within the customer’s ServiceNow instance. Includes:
Now Assist & AI Agents Core Components
Custom Skills via Skill Kit
Predictive Intelligence models
Generative AI Controller components (logging, Now Assist Guardian, Data Privacy, spokes, APIs)
Data at rest remains encrypted and local. Prompts and responses are only transmitted externally for model inference and are protected via TLS 1.2 encryption.
Purple Dotted Line – Customer Instance: Optional/Configurable Components
Includes system settings and plugins that enable or enhance security, privacy, and moderation controls, such as:
Long-Term Memory (AI Agents)
Green Solid Line – Now LLM Service Inference in ServiceNow Compute Hubs
Inference is handled by ServiceNow-operated infrastructure in regional or in-country Compute Hubs.
Includes:
Now LLMs
Now SLMs
Azure AI Service for Now Assist Dynamic Translation
Now Assist Guardian runs in parallel via Now SLM (moderation model)
Green Dotted Line – Now LLM Burst to Azure (ServiceNow-managed Azure vNet (Burst))
If capacity exceeds in-region Compute Hub limits, inference traffic is routed to ServiceNow’s Azure tenant using a ServiceNow-managed private Azure vNet.
There is no public internet exposure.
Models remain hosted and operated by ServiceNow.
This mechanism is used for continuity and capacity management, not model diversity.
Azure bursting is not available to UK and Switzerland in-country hubs or Regulated markets.
Blue Dotted Line – OEM Azure OpenAI (ServiceNow-managed Azure vNet)
Inference is routed to Microsoft-hosted GPT-4.1 or GPT-4.1-mini models via a ServiceNow-managed Azure vNet.
ServiceNow controls the subscription, API keys, and gateway access.
ServiceNow does not host or fine-tune the models. Microsoft owns and operates the underlying model infrastructure.
Red Dotted Line – OEM Google Gemini (ServiceNow-managed Google VPC)
Inference is routed to Vertex AI and Gemini models in Google Cloud via a ServiceNow-managed Google VPC.
Routing is handled through Private Service Connect (PSC).
ServiceNow manages the connector and gateway.
Google owns and operates the models and infrastructure.
No model fine-tuning is performed by ServiceNow.
Yellow Dotted Line – OEM Anthropic Claude via Amazon Bedrock (ServiceNow-managed AWS VPC)
Inference is routed to Amazon Bedrock hosted Anthropic Claude using a ServiceNow-managed AWS VPC.
Routing is done through AWS PrivateLink.
ServiceNow manages the connector and access.
AWS and Anthropic control the models and infrastructure.
White Dotted Line – 3rd Party BYO LLMs (Customer-Managed Endpoints)
Customers may configure external LLMs (such as OpenAI, Claude, Bedrock, Gemini) using the Generic LLM Connector or Now Assist Skill Kit.
Customers are responsible for managing their own endpoints, hosting environment, network isolation, API credentials, usage policies, and compliance governance.
These connections operate entirely outside of the ServiceNow-controlled network boundary.
Teal Dotted Line – ServiceNow AI Development Environment (Training)
Used only when a customer opts in to data sharing.
Filtered AI Content is anonymized and sensitive data-cleansed before being stored.
This environment is physically and logically separate from runtime inference compute.
Hosted in the United States.
Customers from regulated markets (such as FedRAMP, SLED, or non-US customers) are not enrolled.

What is the feature?
External Business Locations enables companies to define and support their franchises, dealerships, independent insurance agents, etc in a single system.
Why did we build it / what pain points does it solve?
External Business Locations are an important part of many industries where companies license their brand to 3rd parties. – Manufacturing (automotive dealerships), Insurance (independent insurance agents), F&B (franchises), Retail (Brick & Mortar, Grocery stores), and hospitality (franchised hotels). Today there is
No easy way to define External Business Locations
No easy way to define staff of a External Business Locations
No easy way to enable External Business Locations to manage their own staff (add, delete)
No easy way to define roles played by the External Business Locations staff (e.g Manager can view all cases at a Franchise, but staff can only view the ones they created)
No easy way for the company to view all the cases created by the External Business Locations
How do we solve these pain points?
With External Business Locations in Tokyo, we change this with an out of the box product offering
Define and register External Business Locations using out of the box data model
Enable External Business Location managers to register and manage their staff
Enable external contributors - External Business Locations staff to create and track cases on behalf of customers using a new External Business Location Support portal
Track products sold and installed at External Business Locations
What value does it provide / why should a customer care?
Shift to digital faster: Define and register external business locations (franchise, dealership, brokerage, etc.) and their staff
Increase CSAT: Enable external business location staff to create and track cases on behalf of customers
Increase efficiency; Track products sold to and installed at external business locations

slides.title: Customer Contract Management
slides.text:
Customer Contract Management
Customer Service Management (CSM)
> Capabilities
> CSM
Verify customer entitlements for service requests
Create contracts or sync externally created contracts via REST APIs
1
2
Improve organizational efficiency through a framework for managing a variety of contracts and entitlements
As consumer and business products and services have become more complex, with a multitude of configuration, service, and delivery options with associated entitlements. Often, customers are unaware of their level of entitled support., and agents don’t have a full view of the contract and entitlements.
For example, entitlements can be number of hours of support, hourly rate for extra support, SLAs, extended warranty, lifespan guarantee and more.
Customer Contracts Data Model is a new foundational data model in CSM to enable customer contract and entitlement management in ServiceNow, either creating directly or bringing contracts created elsewhere into ServiceNow, so agents can see all contracts in a
What problem does this solve?
Businesses offer post-sale support through previously agreed service contracts that outline the promises, terms and conditions to customers.​
Today, many businesses often have such service contracts negotiated individually and created manually. The contract terms are not available in a standardized data format to support post-sales workflows.
Additionally, consumer and business products and services have become more complex, with a multitude of configuration, service, and delivery options with associated entitlements. Often, customers are unaware of their level of entitled support.​
Today, there is no easy way
for contract admins ​
to easily centralize contract data for different product/service types ​
to automate the order-to-contract process​
to enable entitlement checks within post-sale support workflows​
and for agents
to check and verify the different kinds support entitlements for a given customer
Why is it important?
Supporting a customer after a product has been purchased, through customer contracts, is critical to maintain customer satisfaction and loyalty. ​
Not having standardized service contracts, or not delivering the service customers are entitled to consistently, leads to service inefficiencies, revenue leakage and lower customer satisfaction.
How are we solving this?
Define a transactional contract data model that is generic and flexible to capture details for contracts and entitlements,
either directly created in ServiceNow or ones that are synced with external systems of record.
Define contract headers, contract lines and other relevant contract data.
Define entitlements together with contracts, or independently.
Maintain references to Sold Products and Install Base items.
What value does it bring?
Improve organizational efficiency: Provide an enhanced framework for managing contracts and entitlements with varied options
Improve contract admin efficiency: Enable admins to create standardized contracts and entitlements
Increase customer satisfaction: Deliver faster service by quickly and accurately verifying customer contracts and entitlements
Who uses it?
Contract Admins
Customer Service / Field Service / Order Agents
Customers
Terms to use
Customer Contract Data Model
Competitive impact
Flexible data model can support high variability of service contracts and entitlement types can support multiple industries out-of-the-box with low code.
This offers differentiation compared to legacy, rigid capabilities of Salesforce, SAP and other ERPs, but can also coexist as a system of action alongside them.

What is the feature?
Install Base Management is a new feature in the Utah release to support install bases for complex products with component hierarchies
What problem does this solve?
Install Base details for complex products need to capture foundational information like, location, install date, status etc and hierarchical information like child or parent install base items. For example, a parent install base item like an iPhone has, child install base items like (sim card, charger, headphones) etc, so that businesses can track and service each item accurately.
Today, there is no way to:
Capture information like install base status, location etc
Define Hierarchy of install base items
Easily access related information like related parties, contracts
Why is it important?
When businesses cannot easily access all relevant information for an install base, agents need to spend an increased amount time finding the exact installed base item, resulting in slower service and lower customer satisfaction.
Businesses need to track the exact details of each child install base item to ensure they are providing the services promised like repairs or replacements. Not having a way to track the hierarchy means, either businesses are providing services customers are not entitled for, leading to revenue leakage or customers are not receiving the right level of service, leading to lower customer satisfaction.
How are we solving this?
We are expanding the Install Base Data Model to include

Improve CSAT: Maintain a holistic view of the service provided for the install base item

slides.title: Partner Relationship Management: Partner Data Model
slides.text:
Partner Relationship Management: Partner Data Model
Customer Service Management (CSM)
> Capabilities
> CSM
Streamline partner lifecycle management by centralizing partner and program data for easy tracking and access
Enhance visibility and tracking of partner profiles fostering stronger and more productive relationships​
Optimize growth by leveraging a centralized data model to identify high-performing partners and uncover new market opportunities
​
Data model to configure and manage partner profiles for partner collaboration​

What is the feature?
Partner Relationship Management: Partner Data Model is a new feature in SOM Q2 ’25 that allows users to create entities to manage partner profiles, enabling efficient management of key partnerships across resellers, ISVs, and distributors.
What problem does this solve?
Businesses face challenges in managing relationships with a wide range of partners, such as resellers, ISVs, and distributors, without the right tools. This lack of coordination can lead to missed opportunities, inefficiencies, hindered growth, and a poor experience for both customers and partners. There is a clear need for a robust Partner Relationship Management (PRM) system to optimize and enhance partnerships, providing tools and workflows to manage the entire partner lifecycle, ensure continuous engagement, and deliver the right content and support for achieving shared goals.
This feature will allow businesses to create and manage a partner (partner name, contact, region, etc.) as well as partner programs (e.g., reseller program, integrator program).
Today there is no way in ServiceNow to create and manage partner profiles.
Why is it important?
This feature will streamline partner lifecycle management, enabling businesses to efficiently manage relationships from onboarding to ongoing engagement, ensuring long-term success. It enhances partner collaboration by improving communication and coordination, fostering productive partnerships. Additionally, it helps businesses identify and capitalize on growth opportunities, such as high-performing partners or new markets through existing channels.
How are we solving this?
As a channel partner admin, I want to define and manage partner programs and partner characteristics (e.g., industry, region, certification type), so that I can categorize and tailor the experience for each partner according to my organization’s unique business model.
What value does it bring?
Streamline Partner Lifecycle Management: Enable businesses to efficiently manage the entire partner lifecycle, ensuring long-term success
Enhance partner visibility: Improve visibility into partner entities fostering productive partnerships
Optimize growth opportunities: Helps businesses identify and capitalize on growth opportunities, like high-performing partners or new markets through existing channels
Who uses it?
Enterprise partner admin, Enterprise partner manager
Terms to use
Partner relationship management

Competitive impact

slides.title: Embedded Experiences: Web embeddables
slides.text:
Embedded Experiences: Web embeddables
Customer Service Management (CSM)
Embed Case and Service Catalog components on third party websites
Provide low code administration to create and deploy Case and Service Catalog web embeddables
Leverage library of pre-built components to decrease cost of implementation
Simplify self-service experiences on third party websites with web embeddables
1
2

> Capabilities
> CSM
What is the feature?
In the Q3 release, we are introducing Embeddable Experiences, which enable organizations to embed self-service capabilities from ServiceNow on their third party website. It a low code administration that provides high value to customers that have created their own self-service portals.
Embeddable Experiences: web embeddables is will introduce self-service components for case management and catalog. In other releases, we will add more components.
What problem does this solve?
Background - Organizations provide support for a variety of products and services for their customers. Often, these products are from different vendors or in-house applications which typically have their own self-service portals such as ServiceNow customer portal, or an in-house portal .
When a customer needs service, they must navigate to one or more locations for customer support. which contributes to a poor and fragmented experience.
To solve this issue, many organizations have developed extensive self-service portals to support one single customer experience for all the products and services they support. This is a one stop shop for customers to get support with the entire organization. Most organizations already have websites like this in place. An example could be “{organizationname]4me“ such as “Sap4me” or My [organizationname]” such as “MyPromethus” or “Santa Monica digital City Hall”.
Given budgetary pressures and other obstacles (e.g. technical debt, development resource constraints, etc.), they are uninterested in replacing their current solutions.
These organizations need to integrate ServiceNow capabilities into their websites for a better customer experience.
There is no easy way to:
Provide a good Customer experience. - Many organizations, however, rely on a variety of point solutions that require customers to access multiple applications to create a case, view case status, or find a service catalog items.
Integrate ServiceNow self-service capabilities - Organizations need a way to seamlessly integrate with, and display information from, ServiceNow in their own web portals
Customize self-service easily - Integrating an existing self-service portal with third-party applications can be challenging. To provide organizations with additional resources, requires significant technical expertise. This is a drain on developers who are already at capacity supporting other complex projects and is a costly undertaking, too.
Why is it important?
Organizations need to provide their customers with a single view for self-service to streamline their experience in a single location.
Organizations need an easy way to configure and integrate with ServiceNow with a low code/no code solution using out of the box components web embeddables. These components should be easy to deploy.
Also, organizations want to quickly make changes to existing web embeddables without heavy customizations
How are we solving this?
Embedded Experiences: web embeddables will:
Provide easy setup experiences to configure embeddable componentsand generate code for deployment.
Include simple administration with a low code/no code setup.
Out of the box web embeddables with capabilities such as case management (Q3), playbooks(later release) and service catalog (later release). These ready-made embedded capabilities will let organizations easily make changes while minimizing the need for developers to spend countless hours re-engineering their customer service solution.
What value does it bring?
Streamline customer experience: Reduce the effort for customers to self-serve with ServiceNow capabilities on third party websites
Faster time to market: Provide a low code/no code administration for creating and deploying ServiceNow embedded experiences
Reduce customization costs: Leverage ServiceNow user interface components to easily compose, edit web components to deploy on third party websites
Who uses it?
Customers will be able to access ServiceNow capabilities from third party websites.
Administrators will configure web embeddables with a low code solution and generate code for the organizations web developers to deploy on their website.
Developers will have a low code way to create, modify and deploy web embeddables.
Terms to use
Embeddables: Commonly used term to refer to applications embedded as an element of a host web page and are substantially independent of the page itself; provides users of the host page access to content from another source.
Embedded Experiences: is the ServiceNow unofficial name. Embedded experiences or web widgets, is a term used to describe a feature, capability, or application integrated into a third party website, such as organization website, that is substantially independent of that website itself. The embedded component provides users of the third party site access to resources or information from ServiceNow
web embeddables: web embeddables are macroponents that can be embedded in third party websites (organization websites) with ServiceNow capabilities such as case list, case view, case create, etc. using UI Builder on the Now Platform.
Release Details
Embeddable Experiences: web embeddables will be part of the Q3 Xanadu release and the standard SKU. A web embeddable case or catalog component will also use portal visit counts. These self-service components (e.g. a list of cases that would normally be on a portal page) are now embedded on non-servicenow AKA our customers website (external website). Therefore, it will be counted as views (on that external website) just as if the user was on a portal page. The web embeddables will use that same portal usage metering.

Agents currently face delays and inefficiencies due to navigating multiple tabs and scattered data when trying to understand customer case history. Today, agents have to go through multiple clicks to find the customer. history buried in a case. This is inefficient and many agents will simply not use the customer history to provide service or a solution. This means customers are getting less contextual and less personalized service.
Business Need
Reduced context switching and cognitive load for agents
Boosts agent productivity by reducing time spent on gathering information ​
Supports responsive layouts for side panels and contextual views ​

Ability to adjust the time grouping to monthly and quarterly for date filter​
Ability to configure milestones, their icons, and branding by admins and customers​
Ability to configure activity and display by updated date
By building Customer History as an independent, reusable, and responsive component with: ​
In-line filtering and search functionality ​
Toggleable facet vs filter view (via new UIB property) ​
Customizable UI via UI Builder ​
Step-by-step guided setup for quick and consistent configuration ​
Dynamic refresh to ensure data is up to date ​

> CSM

2
3
Talk Track
Summary
Within Customer Access Management, responsibilities are used to govern what a user with a specific relationship will have access to. The specifics of that access are determined through responsibility configurations. While the concept of responsibility access configurations had been introduced in earlier releases, we removed the ability to edit them in Yokohama to address some security needs and additional enhancements. Responsibility access configurations are now editable in Zurich, with an initial focus on account team member access configurations. As an example, we ship an out of the box responsibility called “account manager.” A user can be given the account manager responsibility for a specific account. The responsibility is configured to let that user see account information as well as the account’s install base details.
Chargeable
Standard
Challenge
Managing access for different relationships previously required scripting, requiring customization for any edits to OOTB responsibilities and making it generally more difficult for administrators to create new responsibilities for CAM. Especially as we expand in CRM, this means more data entities, more personas, and more relationships. Managing access to customer data for all these users, internal or external, requires a scalable, configurable approach, which the declarative framework provides with a UI-based configuration experience and powerful filtering and mapping capabilities.
Business Need
Solution
Administrators can now use responsibility access configurations to specify the role required to access specific table entities, and at what level. With new filters and table mappings, administrators now have the flexibility to model very detailed relationships to capture all of the different types of responsibilities that might exist.
Target Persona(s)
Admins
