Talk track:
Banks that use the ServiceNow AI Platform can continuously implement new processes and innovate faster. When banks configure a business process on the ServiceNow AI Platform, they start from a high level of pre-built capabilities. And as a result, Banks lower their cost to serve, while driving business value in weeks, not years
Banks of all sizes and structures have used ServiceNow to drive value quickly - as seen above, small banks have deployed ServiceNow across their business in days, and large banks have simplified processes in weeks.
Our banking customers have... 1) serviced customers quickly with automated issue resolution 2) simplified self-service 3) and decreased manual workloads across onboarding, servicing and exceptions processes. And they have revamped these processes FAST. Lloyds, for example, reinvented 7 payment processes within 12 weeks, BMO received 2x platform adoption in 2 months, and Bridgewater went from concept to launch-ready in less than 1 week.
Ultimately, this all helps banks compete on customer experience, as so much of their differentiation in the Banking market is experience-driven.
Some customers may find “12 weeks” unrealistic as a claim, as it sounds risky. ServiceNow is uniquely able to drive business value while controlling risks. We do so by:
minimizing data security risk (we don’t have to hold the data)
minimizing change management (minimal employee enablement is necessary, due to the supportive nature of the applications) and
ensuring compliance is built into each process, and anticipating the needs for assurance.
We also calibrate the speed of implementation to the timeline of the customer.
CUSTOMER DETAIL
We have capabilities on our platform to digitize business problems across complex banking processes, and we have worked with a wide array of financial institutions to solve their unique problems and drive impact across their businesses.
Lloyds Banking Group (LBG):
Company Background: In March 2020, the impact of COVID-19 disrupted LBG’s existing, manual labor intensive processes, leaving the company with potentially increased operational costs and heightened complexity. Back-office operations relied on manual processes requiring hundreds of staff to deal with individual customer payment requests and payment issues. LBG’s payments operations processes were therefore challenged with delivering higher levels of automation and efficiency. This was not only in response to the challenges of new working models enforced by COVID-19 but also sustaining the service customers expect, supporting the UK economy and helping the country recover. As the scale of digital payments continues to grow, efficiency through innovation and automation has become paramount. Since July 2020, LBG has used agile SAFE methodology to transform payment operations processes. By prioritising outcomes, challenging ways of working in operations and exploiting data driven process automation through ServiceNow’s Financial Service Operations platform, nine processes have been revolutionised. Furthermore, seven of these payment operations processes were transformed in just 12 weeks.The Problem - Payment In Error: If a customer makes an error when making a payment, such as getting the payee details wrong, they must contact the bank to begin the process of trying to recover the money. There were up to 450,000 individual cases each year, each one requiring a front-end staff member to open the case use manually obtained data from other systems so that the middle office could correct the payment and recover the funds through manual actions. In 12 weeks, LBG reviewed the manual steps required within the process and those of value were digitised by integrating with systems of record and automating the case through process automation. By validating data at the first point of contact with the system of record, the failure demand has significantly decreased, improving service to customers.The Solution: 72% automation of Payment in Error process (from 100% manual in the back office, requiring much less human interaction, affecting 450,000 cases per year)
Bank of Montreal (BMO)
Bank of Montreal, one of the Big Five Banks in Canada, was challenged to transform their digital experiences.The Problem: Outdated technology leads to a host of challenges, and Bank of Montreal was experiencing a lack of effective self-servicing for customers, high operating costs, a complicated customer communications process requiring numerous touchpoints and manual work from employees, and a lack of metrics and insights which made it nearly impossible to improve processes to be more cost effective and customer accommodating.
The Solution : 63% reduction in case types across every business facing support group, going from 2,500 to 400.
BMO’s customer self-servicing, employee experiences, and reporting all greatly improved by simply reducing case types. This became a reality because the ServiceNow AI Platform made it easy for the BMO IT team to rationalize and simplify.
For the customers, the simple reduction in case types made self-service an appealing and efficient option, as opposed to overwhelming. They now had uncomplicated self-servicing options, and they no longer needed to search through a catalog of 2,500 items to submit a form. Now, there were fewer catalog items, fewer forms, and an easier, more intuitive UX to submit requests. Customers could now easily self-serve areas such as update their account information, transfer money, submit a loan application, search for a local branch, and much more.
For employees, the reduction in case types allowed them to spend more of their time on more value-driving work, rather than becoming overwhelmed with service requests Service representatives can spend less time on questions/issues, service calls, emails.. As a result, employees can focus on more meaningful work, leaving BMO with a large reduction in operating expenses.
This all led to stronger analysis and insights for the business. With a much better understanding of what customers were asking, when they were asking, and if/how cases were being resolved, BMO could identify patterns far more easily and implement changes to improve customer service. For example, BMO could begin to benchmark behaviors, such as, “customers in the first 60 days tend to experience the following challenges. Here is what we are going to have product offering wise for that segment.”
Another large benefit ServiceNow has provided BMO was the easy implementation and adoptability across initiatives. The platform saw 2X adoption within just 12 months, thanks to the clear value-add as well as the intuitive nature of the technology.
Bridgewater Bank:
Company Background: Bridgewater Bank understands what it takes to keep a small business running. It’s a local bank serving businesses throughout the Twin Cities area of Minnesota with financial services that include lending, financing, and business banking.
The Problem: As a growing bank, Bridgewater typically used manual processes to manage workflows. Place used a simple spreadsheet to keep track of what loans his officers were processing and the status of each loan. When passing customer information among groups, loan officers emailed relevant information to other teams. While each officer had their methods for tracking work, there was no central system.
“As we’ve grown and hired more loan officers, it’s become harder to maintain visibility into all phases of lending,” says Bridgewater Banking leader. “When we started processing PPP loans, I’d spend two to three hours every day trying to track the status of all loans in process. Given the constant changes and how fast everyone was working, our tracking spreadsheets would be quickly outdated.”
The Solution: With the Small Business Loan Management solution, Bridgewater achieves a low portfolio risk since it works within the existing lending process. The bank now has one location for loan, credit, and administrative teams to find information about customers and loans. Teams no longer need to interrupt busy loan officers to ask about a customer. Instead, they can check on loan progress in real time, look up contact information, and follow up with requests for additional information.
Several integrations make the Small Business Loan Management solution more useful and simpler for Bridgewater. The app uses single sign-on with Azure Active Directory. A streamlined Google Form allows customers to start an inquiry for PPP loans directly through the Bridgewater website. Information is automatically pulled into a customer record in the Small Business Loan Management solution, at which point Place can easily review the inquiry and assign it to a loan officer based on each officer’s specialty or workload. The app makes it easier for loan officers to stay organized, contributing to a reduction of up to 48% in workload per case file. It also reduces time usually spent by Place in manually updating loan status or passing customers to additional teams. For customers, the solution means that teams spend less time asking for redundant information, leading to a more streamlined, less stressful lending experience.
And this was all achieved at speed – the Small Business Loan Management solution from concept to launch-ready in less than a week.

​​
Solution​​
Accelerate service management across your ecosystem by connecting ServiceNow Instances with Service Bridge.

Diagnose and repair service issues framework
Telecommunications Services Mgmt (TSM)
> Capabilities
> TSM
Resolve network issues faster with smarter, standardized diagnostics built for telco
Standardizes diagnostics using TMF-compliant APIs across telco systems
Speeds up MTTR with AI-powered analysis and root cause insights
Empowers agents and customers through self-service testing tools
Reduces escalations by enabling lower-tier support to run advanced diagnostics
1
2
3
4
Powered by Now Assist
Summary​​
ServiceNow’s Diagnose and repair service issues framework is a centralized, industry-standardized capability that streamlines network issue detection and resolution for telco providers. It allows both human agents and AI agents to initiate, automate, and analyze network diagnostics via a standardized API—directly from incidents, service orders, or customer portals.
Originally tied to customer service problem cases, it now extends across incidents, changes, orders, and orchestration workflows, enabling proactive diagnostics at every layer of service operations
Chargeable​​
Professional
Challenge​​
Previously, agent teams relied on fragmented diagnostic processes. Each team had to log into separate subsystems, like OSS tools, and manually run diagnostics, often with inconsistent methods and no shared standards. This lack of integration with service management workflows led to delays and inefficiencies.
These delays often resulted in high operational costs, as basic diagnostics needed to be escalated to senior technical teams. Frontline agents lacked the tools or insights to resolve issues independently, and this created unnecessary handoffs and higher support costs.
Business Need​​
Fragmented Diagnostic Processes Teams previously had to log into individual subsystems (e.g. OSS tools) manually to run diagnostics. Diagnostics weren’t connected to service management workflows, creating silos and delays.
High Costs from Escalations Basic diagnostics required escalation to higher-tier (and more expensive) technical teams. Frontline agents lacked tools or insights to resolve issues quickly. Lack of early diagnostic automation increased operational overhead.
Solution​​
Industry Standard, Unified Diagnostics The framework delivers a unified, standardized approach to diagnostics using industry-conformant APIs. By centralizing and standardizing diagnostics across tools and teams, it removes the guesswork and complexity of traditional troubleshooting.
Faster Issue Resolution (MCCR & FCR Improvements) This solution improves mean time to resolution (MTTR) and first-call resolution (FCR) by empowering agents and AI to automatically execute tests and summarize logs. With diagnostic insights embedded into workflows, agents no longer need to escalate as frequently to higher teams, and they can resolve issues faster using structured insights.
The framework supports a shift-left operations model. Frontline agents now have access to diagnostic tools and summarized logs that were previously available only to more technical teams. This reduces operational costs and boosts service team productivity.
Shift-Left Operational Model, Self-Service Empowerment End customers are also empowered with self-service capabilities. Guided forms in the customer portal allow them to initiate diagnostics themselves, which reduces support call volumes and enables faster, more satisfying resolutions. These diagnostics can also auto-classify issues and route them to the appropriate fulfillment or remediation workflows.
Extensible Across Domains The framework is designed to be extensible across domains. While it began in service assurance, it now supports diagnostics during order orchestration and change execution as well. It can be triggered from incidents, alerts, or fulfillment activities, making it a scalable solution across the telco service lifecycle.
​​
Target Persona(s) ​
Service and Network Operations Leaders, Telco Service Providers CSPs MSPs using ServiceNow TSM

The Telecom discovery builder framework facilitates rapid, no-code development of new discovery Service Graph Connectors and includes out-of-the-box data source validation tools.
Chargeable​​
Entitled to TSOM Professional & Visibility SKU; requires TSOM Professional & Visibility license
Challenge​​
Telecom networks rely on integrating with hundreds of vendor equipment providers (OEM - Original Equipment Manufacturers, vendor EMS - Equipment Management Systems, or NMS - Network Management Systems) to keep inventory systems synchronized with live network resource data and prevent configuration item (CI) drift. Currently, network engineers must collaborate with software engineering teams to develop and maintain discovery interfaces—a process that is time-consuming, inefficient, and resource-intensive. This traditional approach leads to delays in enabling network visibility, ongoing maintenance burdens, and challenges in maintaining reliable data quality.
Business Need​​
Current manual, code-heavy processes for building and maintaining discovery interfaces are slow, inefficient, and prone to delays. Engineering teams need no-code solutions to accelerate development, reduce maintenance efforts, and a means to ensure data quality.
​​
Solution​​
​​To address these challenges, engineering teams or integration partners with domain knowledge of vendor equipment data need a no-code solution that simplifies the creation of new discovery interfaces, minimizes maintenance efforts, and a means to ensure the quality of discovered data. This approach accelerates time-to-market for new interfaces while significantly reducing development costs.
The Telecom discovery builder framework facilitates rapid, no-code development of new discovery Service Graph Connectors and includes out-of-the-box data source validation tools. This ensures a significantly reduced effort for anyone looking to onboard a new Service Graph Connector into the platform, accelerating time-to-market and reducing development costs.

Challenge​​
Discovering the logical network topology in a Nokia Altiplano multi-vendor Passive Optical Network (PON) environment is complex due to the heterogeneous mix of vendor-specific equipment and interfaces. Network engineers face challenges integrating with diverse data models, fragmented protocols, multiple vendor instances, and maintaining consistent, accurate inventory of logical network resources. This lack of reliable, end-to-end network visibility hampers troubleshooting efforts, slows issue resolution, and complicates network planning and capacity management.

This comprehensive solution streamlines logical network mapping, enhances troubleshooting efficiency, and supports better network planning and capacity management.

Talk Track
Summary​​
​​CDMB classes for data center power management equip engineers with a suite of capabilities for real-time monitoring and efficient management of power-related equipment, facilitating rapid response to outages, proactive communication with impacted customers, and optimizing power utilization for continuous operations.
Chargeable​​
CMDB classes are included with CMDB Class Models. Entitled to TNI Pro; requires TNI Pro license. Proactive Service Experience requires TSM.
Challenge​​
Managing data center power is complex due to diverse equipment, shared power connections, and the significant heat generated by operations. Without tools to monitor both power usage and thermal metrics, overheating risks increase, leading to inefficiencies, outages, and higher costs. Engineers also need a way to quickly pinpoint issues or potential risks to ensure reliable and scalable operations while proactively addressing these challenges.
Business Need​​
Engineers require a robust solution to manage the growing complexity of power and cooling systems within data centers and network sites. They need real-time visibility into equipment health and the ability to model power equipment and relationships to understand the impact of outages.
​​
Solution​​
The CMDB classes for data center power management capability provide engineers with essential tools to model, group, manage, and monitor all types of data center equipment. It offers a comprehensive view of facility power systems, enabling real-time health monitoring with insights into thermal and power metrics. Configuring shared power connections between equipment allows for quick assessment of the impacts of outages, ensuring engineers can efficiently mitigate risks, optimize power usage, and maintain uninterrupted operations. Additionally, the ability to group racks enables tailored access control, ensuring owners can securely manage and monitor only their designated racks.
Integrating with Telecom Service Management (TSM), this solution stands out by enabling proactive customer communication. By leveraging insights from power incidents and changes, it proactively notifies customers about potential service impacts, protecting their business operations. This not only ensures uninterrupted operations but also builds customer trust through increased transparency and timely responsiveness.
Comprehensive facility visibility: Model all types of data center power equipment to gain a complete view of facility infrastructure, empowering engineers to make well-informed decisions.
Faster outage impact analysis: Model and visualize shared power connections between equipment to quickly understand the cascading effects of power outages and reduce downtime.
Improved access control: Enable the creation of customized rack groups, allowing owners to securely access and manage only their specific group of racks, enhancing security and efficiency.
Proactive monitoring: Monitor data center power equipment health in real time, leveraging detailed insights into power and thermal metrics to prevent issues and optimize performance.
Proactive customer communication: Harness power incident and change insights to proactively notify customers about service impacts, safeguarding their operations and fostering trust through enhanced transparency and responsiveness.
Target Persona(s) ​
Facility Agent, NOC agent, SOC agent Telecom Network Inventory SSC product page: https://servicenow.seismic.com/Link/Content/DCX34p4HBX46P8MQJdBBT3Cj3GMV

Summary​​
Floor map visualization with metric overlay empowers engineers to design, maintain, and optimize their network sites and data center infrastructure efficiently while delivering high-quality performance and staying cost-effective.
Chargeable​​
Professional. Entitled to TNI Pro & Indoor Mapping Service SKU; requires TNI Pro & Indoor Mapping Service SKU license.
Challenge​​
Data centers and network sites are inherently complex, hosting floors of equipment racks and millions of miles of cables spread across numerous site locations. Effective management of equipment across these sites is vital to ensure seamless operations, scalability, and reliability. Additionally, data center growth is exploding around the world, fueled by the growth of data and AI. Network and data center operators need the ability to track and manage their operational environments, monitor their equipment, identify incidents, changes, or alarms, and quickly correlate performance degradation with impacted customers. Without comprehensive and precise network site and data center management, it is challenging to design and maintain infrastructure accurately, deliver reliable performance, and optimize energy consumption. Accurate site management and analysis are crucial for running infrastructure with quality performance and at optimal cost.
Business Need​​
Engineers face the challenge of managing highly complex data centers and numerous network sites. Effective oversight is critical to ensure seamless operations, avoid downtime, and scale infrastructure to meet growing demands. Engineers need tools to visualize and manage equipment and floor layouts, monitor real-time health metrics, quickly identify issues, and optimize capacity allocation to enhance performance, reduce costs, and maintain optimal utilization.
​​
Solution​​
Floor map visualization with metric overlay empowers engineers to tackle the intricate challenges of managing network equipment across a multitude of data center floors and network sites. With accurate equipment and layout visualization and color-coded health status, engineers can monitor equipment, identify performance bottlenecks, address incidents promptly, and plan for future growth. This streamlined approach ensures efficient resource utilization and allocation, reduced operational costs, and improved service delivery.
Visual floor mapping: Maintain detailed network site and data center equipment floor maps, giving engineers accurate visual access to equipment and layout.
Real-time health: View data center floor and equipment health metrics with a color-coded display for alerts, incidents, and performance monitoring.
Enhanced operational efficiency: Quickly identify and resolve issues to meet SLAs and improve operational performance.
Capacity optimization: Optimize site and data center floor space and capacity planning to ensure optimal allocation of resources.
This solution enables engineers to design, maintain, and optimize their network sites and data center infrastructure efficiently while delivering high-quality performance and staying cost-effective. Whether tracking growth, enhancing scalability, or minimizing downtime, this solution ensures your network sites and data centers remain future-proof and highly reliable.

ServiceNow Sales and Order Management for Telecom (SOMT) empowers organizations to define new product and service offerings quickly, streamline
complex sales and order fulfillment processes, and easily manage post-sales activities to grow services revenue, reduce costs and elevate customer experience. SOMT ensures seamless, sales and
order management processes across all products and lines of business lines with a flexible, catalog-driven architecture. It delivers a distinct competitive edge across the entire value chain—from
prospecting and capturing sales to fulfilling and managing orders.
Here’s the value that SOMT delivers across each step of the process:
Prospect - Identify customer needs, create opportunities, and manage
Identifying prospective customers for the wide range of products and services that modern tech providers offer today can be both challenging and time consuming. SOMT helps to easily identify
potential customers and assign them to the right agents to qualify and covert into prospective customers by targeting the right set of products or services to precisely meet needs.
Propose - Build quotes, manage revisions, and automatically convert quotes to orders
SOMT helps to price and quote services by assisting agents with the required data configuration needed to contextually propose offerings and then triggering workflows to further qualify, and design
the request as the sale progresses. With real time data, SOMT also helps in the quoting process by enabling agents to skillfully negotiate and offer suitable discounts and promotions to offer pricing
aimed at converting quotes to orders.
Capture - Capture orders using a single guided user workspace, and quickly re-bundle and update product offerings
Following quote qualification, order capture will enhance the order by incorporating relevant details like installation times that align with customer requirements and field agent availability, as well as
technical design specifications. Based on specific rules, such as, complex orders or high touch customer interactions will trigger the creation and integration with project management delivered by
ServiceNow’s Strategic Portfolio Management.
Fulfill - Automate the decomposition and fulfillment of product, service, and resource orders
After an order is qualified, a decomposition of the order will occur to determine the base elements of the order, this is the services/resources involved in the delivery of the order (aka the Bill of
material/BOM). This decomposition is performed iteratively as designs are performed and data is discovered. The order can then be fulfilled across a collection of actors and applications including
field services, IT/Engineering delivery applications, an ecosystem of partners, testing processes and revenue assurance applications.
Manage - Track assigned fulfillment tasks and manage post-sales activities
After completing an order, it's essential to support the customer for any future changes they may need. This could include adding more products to increase
revenue, managing existing products for tasks like renewals or replacements, relocating, downsizing, or temporarily suspending services. SOMT offers an efficient solution for all these scenarios.

Succinct benefit or value prop for the persona buyer

Summary​​
The Lead-to-Cash Command Center is a centralized hub that unifies opportunities, quotes, contracts, and orders from disparate systems into a single, hierarchical view. This feature provides real-time visibility into every critical milestone, from order capture to invoicing and delivery, helping contract admins and sales managers streamline their workflows. By consolidating data from CPQ, ERP, and other systems, it enhances operational efficiency, reduces manual work, and ensures timely revenue recognition, ultimately boosting productivity and minimizing financial risks.
Chargeable​​
Available with SOM Pro
Challenge​​
Managing and consolidating data from multiple siloed systems, such as orders in SAP, quotes in Tacton, and contracts in separate ERP platforms.
Teams struggling with switching between systems, manually consolidating updates, and missing key milestones that impact revenue recognition.
Lack of real-time visibility into every critical milestone from order capture to invoicing and delivery.
Inefficient workflows and increased manual work leading to operational inefficiencies and financial risks.
Business Need​​
Boost operational productivity by centralizing data and reducing manual work.
Enhance real-time visibility into critical milestones, ensuring timely revenue recognition.
Streamline workflows and minimize financial risks by identifying delays and bottlenecks early.
Improve collaboration and communication among teams, leading to better decision-making.
Optimize revenue recognition and drive operational efficiency throughout the lead-to-cash process.
​​
Solution​​
The Lead-to-Cash Command Center works by acting as a centralized hub that unifies opportunities, quotes, contracts, and orders from disparate systems into a single, hierarchical view. It pulls data from CPQ, ERP, and other systems, presenting it in a tree-like structured format that is both visual and interactive. Solid lines represent hard, user-defined linkages, while dotted lines represent soft, database-inferred associations, which can be easily converted between. At the heart of this feature is the Order to Cash (OTC) object, a new record type in ServiceNow, which acts as a central node for managing linked opportunities, quotes, orders, and contracts. Users can track and manage tasks, emails, attachments, and checklists at the OTC record level, ensuring a comprehensive and streamlined management process.
Target Persona(s) ​
Product catalog administrators
Order operations
Sales operations
Revenue operations

Case Management for Order Operations
Streamline order exceptions by handling many changes per case via case lines
Improve customer satisfaction by ensuring issues are resolved quickly, preventing delays
Increase operational efficiency by avoiding bottlenecks and disruptions in order processing workflow
Reduce operational costs by streamlining exception handling to minimize shipping and return processing expenses
1

> MCO
This feature lets customers submit cases against one or more lines in an order to handle deviations from standard workflows due to exceptions, such as expedited shipping requests or changes in quantity.
This feature includes creating a new order case type with order or order lines as case lines. Agents will be able to create a case and add the order lines for which they are requesting a changes. The agent will then work through the case, and as needed create case tasks for other team members or assign case lines to others agents.
This feature will reduce order delays, improve customer satisfaction and avoid extra costs from mistakes or returns. By handling order exceptions well, businesses can build trust with customers, and gain customer loyalty.
Case lines and case line characteristics, case line tasks are being introduced in the Q4 release and we will be leveraging those capabilities for this feature. So to learn more about this horizontal feature please do attend the MCO deep dive scheduled for later this month.
What is the feature?
Case Management for Order Operations is a new feature in MCO Q4 ’24 that lets customers submit cases against one or more lines in an order to handle deviations from standard workflows due to exceptions, such as expedited shipping requests or changes in quantity.
What problem does this solve?
Businesses encounter order issues due to inventory discrepancies, payment processing problems, shipping and delivery errors etc. They can also result from customer input mistakes, such as entering incorrect information, or changes in customer needs such as faster shipping, or quantity changes. These issues disrupt the normal flow of order processing and need to be addressed to ensure smooth operations and maintain customer satisfaction.
Today there is no way in ServiceNow to reference whole orders, or specific line items in an order to submit a case against.
Why is it important?
Having a smooth order exception process is important to identify and address problems quickly when something goes wrong with an order, or handle customer requests for change as much as possible. This can reduce order delays, improve customer satisfaction and avoid extra costs from mistakes or returns. By handling order exceptions well, businesses can build trust with customers, and gain customer loyalty.
How are we solving this?
Add multiple order lines, and specific issues per line on order exception case e.g new order qty, New ship date​
Collaborate, create tasks and assign tasks for specific lines​
Check eligibility for change order such as order fulfilment state and if approved​
Update the order lines internally or in external systems e.g SAP​
What value does it bring?
Higher customer satisfaction: Ensure that issues are resolved quickly, preventing delays and maintaining customer trust and satisfaction
Higher operational efficiency: Avoid bottlenecks and disruptions in order processing workflow by managing exceptions quickly
Reduce operational costs: Reduce expenses such as additional shipping costs or return processing costs by streamlining exception handling
Who uses it?
Order agents, Fulfillment agents

slides.text:
Manufacturing Commercial Operations (MCO)
> Capabilities
Central hub of information from multiple systems to streamline lead-to-cash journey​
Boost operational productivity with centralizing data, reduced swivel chairing and streamlined workflows​
Reduce financial risk and operational impact with a hierarchical view that helps identify delays or issues early​
Prevent revenue leakage through proactive resolution of milestone delays to ensure timely revenue recognition
1
2
3
Lead-to-Cash Process Management
Professional
> MCO
Talk Track:​
This feature is going to act as a centralized hub that unifies opportunities, quotes, contracts, and orders from these disparate systems into a single, hierarchical view.​
​
Think of it as a control tower for your entire fulfillment journey. It gives contract admins and sales managers real-time visibility into every critical milestone — from order capture to invoicing and delivery. It pulls data from CPQ, ERP, and other systems, presenting it in a tree-like structured format that’s both visual and interactive -- to show how everything is connected. Solid lines represent hard, user-defined linkages, and dotted lines represent soft, database-inferred associations. You can convert between them easily, which gives you the flexibility to manage relationships without sacrificing clarity. ​
Please note that this feature assumes that data is imported into ServiceNow from external systems, with integration partners handling the data flow. These partners handle the mapping and importing of data from external systems into ServiceNow. ​
By providing a comprehensive view of the order fulfillment journey, this feature helps organizations identify potential delays or bottlenecks early on, allowing them to take proactive measures to mitigate risks and ensure on-time delivery. Ultimately, this plays a critical role in optimizing revenue recognition and driving operational efficiency throughout the lead to cash process.​
What is the feature?​
Order to Cash Operations: Lead-to-Cash Command Center is a new feature in MCO Q3 ’25 that creates an unified and hierarchical interface to manage orders, quotes, opportunities, and contracts across different systems. ​
What problem does this solve?​
Many organizations rely external systems to import transactional data and manage day to day transactions. Some of them could include importing orders and contracts from SAP, quotes from Tacton and other ERP solutions. They need a unified workspace that bridges the gap between orders captured in CPQ systems like Tacton and back-end systems like SAP. This will ensure that businesses can streamline their sales process, ensuring clarity and coordination throughout the order fulfillment journey.​
The feature aims to consolidate data from various third party systems into a unified view for contract admins and sales managers. This helps manage orders, quotes, opportunities, and contracts efficiently. The Lead to cash Command Center gives teams a real-time, consolidated view of everything happening across the fulfillment lifecycle — from order capture to delivery, install, and invoicing. Think of it as a control tower for operations. It pulls data from systems like CPQ, ERP, to track key milestones, identify delays, and surface bottlenecks. ​
Users create an Order to Cash (OTC) record for a specific account by selecting a business process and linking it to relevant opportunities, quotes, or orders. This record acts as a centralized hub to manage associated tasks, data, and milestones.​
The feature includes a hierarchical nodal map view, displaying relationships between different records. Hard linkages (user-defined associations) are shown with solid lines, while soft linkages (database associations) are indicated by dotted lines. Users can convert hard linkages to soft linkages and vice versa, offering flexibility in managing these relationships.​
At the OTC record level, users can track and manage tasks, emails, attachments, and checklists. They can also view detailed information for each associated entity (e.g., opportunity, quote, or order), along with any related activities and documents. Additionally, customers can define user-defined checklists to track important milestones for better progress monitoring.​
This feature streamlines the management of opportunities, quotes, orders, and related tasks, enabling users to track the status and progress of each associated entity in one unified view.​
The feature assumes that data is imported into ServiceNow from external systems, with integration partners handling the data flow. These partners handle the mapping and importing of data from external systems into ServiceNow. So currently, the OTC record is a new ServiceNow record type that aggregates various records within the MCO ecosystem, enabling a single comprehensive view.​
Why is it important?​
The feature, lead to cash Command Center, was created to address the challenge of managing and consolidating data from multiple segregated systems. Specifically, it was built to help major customers like Siemens, who have orders, quotes, and opportunities spread across different systems to have a unified view and manage these records efficiently.​
The OTC feature enhances operational efficiency by centralizing data, reducing manual work and system-switching errors, while its hierarchical view enables early detection of delays to reduce risk. It also helps prevent revenue leakage by proactively tracking milestones to ensure timely and accurate revenue recognition.​
How are we solving this?​
Here are some expected capabilities of the command center:​
Ability for a Contract admin to be able to create and view OTC records​
Gives a visibility into opportunities, quotes, orders, opportunity lines, quote lines, order lines contracts, and invoices that need immediate attention from multiple systems tied to OTC record​
Present data in a tree like structured format (OTC and related child objects) and also be able to search a specific entity type​
A contract admin/Sales Manager should be able to create checklists tied to OTC record and sales representative should only be able to view them​
Ability to consolidate the tasks from multiple records (open orders/opportunities etc) and display them for the chosen OTC node on nodal map view​
Ability to consolidate emails from multiple related records ( opportunity/orders etc) tied to an OTC object​
An OTC admin should also be able to compose an email tied to an OTC object.​
Team communication and sidebar discussion should also happen for an OTC object for contract Admin to discuss with stakeholders.​
Ability to view all related attachments from orders/leads/quotes under a single subtab instead of multiple documents​
Ability to do a soft and hard linkage associations tied to OTC record.​
Ability to delink an association of an entity to an OTC record​
What value does it bring?​
Prevent revenue leakage through proactive resolution of milestone delays to ensure timely revenue recognition​
Who uses it?​
Contract Admin, Sales Manager, Sales representative​

Change Requester

Cloud Infrastructure Change Model

Change Management Process
Let’s walk through the change lifecycle in two scenarios
- The first will be a typical normal change
- The second will leverage ServiceNow’s modern change capabilities showcasing the use of change models, dynamic risk assessment, change approval policies, success scores, and flows.
Scenario 1: Normal Change
Show at the top is a timeline of a normal ITIL mode 1 change that involves numerous manual steps and, usually, a long lead time to complete the process from beginning to end. It’s a ‘one size fits all’ approach, which at times can be inefficient for certain use cases.
<CLICK> In the ‘New’ state, this is where the Change Requester creates the Change and all details are filled in manually
Service Impact is determined by inspecting the dependency map.
Implementation Plan, Backout Plan, Testing Plan, and Risk & Impact Assessment fields are filled out.
To evaluate risk, a Risk Assessment questionnaire is answered. These questionnaires, while useful, can be a bit subjective as questions can sometimes be open to interpretation or answered in such a way as to purposely drive a low-risk outcome, to avoid scrutiny.
<CLICK> Once the details are complete, the change is sent for 1st line approval and moved to the ‘Assess’ state
The Change Approver reviews the change for technical accuracy and change compliance.
If all looks good the change is approved. If not, the change is rejected, and the requester will need to make the necessary updates.
If the change risk is High, the change will be sent to the CAB for authorization. This could entail additional delays waiting for the CAB meeting to occur.
<CLICK> Once CAB authorizes the change, the change moves to ‘Scheduled’ state where it will remain until the scheduled start date
At Planned Start Date/Time the change can be moved to ‘Implement’, where implementation activities can begin under the coordination of the Change Implementer and change tasks can be completed by assigned groups.
Once implementation is complete, the change is reviewed and the outcome (success or otherwise) captured in the Close code and Close notes.
As you can see, and likely relate to, this is a very manual and time-consuming process. Is there a better way? Yes!
For changes that are frequently implemented, with risk that is well understood, and with implementation steps well documented, tested, and have a proven history of success, it is much more efficient to have a tailored process where only the necessary states and transitions are required.
Let’s look at such an example for Cloud Infrastructure Provisioning changes.
Scenario 2: Cloud Infrastructure Change Model
Shown at the very bottom of this slide is the timeline of a mode 2 Cloud Infrastructure Provisioning change leveraging a fit-for-purpose change model
This model can be used for provisioning new cloud infrastructure (e.g. New EC2 instance) which is usually a templated, automated process using cloud provisioning tools.
With Change Models a change manager can create a tailored, automated change process which is fit-for-purpose, without any customization effort. There is no need for a ServiceNow admin to create a new workflow or update/add to the change workflow.
This saves time and effort for the Change Requester, Change Approver and Change Implementer, while providing the Change Manager with right level of governance and change control without adding unnecessary overhead.
Existing change workflow remains unaffected and can continue to function as is, while the new model, flows and approval policies operate in parallel.
Models allow the change manager to define the transition conditions i.e. what are the mandatory fields that need to be completed at each state? Once the transition conditions are met, the change can move automatically from one state to the next.
<CLICK> New change is created from the Cloud Infrastructure change model with fields automatically pre-filled (e.g. Configuration Item, Assignment Group, Category etc.) per the change model
With ITSM Pro, there is no need to manual answer Risk Assessment questions. Change Risk can be calculated automatically, based on historical data, using risk intelligence machine learning to predict the risk.
<CLICK> Once all the details are populated, the change can be submitted for approval where next steps will be determined via applied change approval policies.
Change Approval Policies use decision tables to determine whether the change can be auto-approved, auto-rejected, or sent for manual approval, based on the policy input data (conflicts, change risk, team change success scores, change model success, etc.)
In this example, because the Assignment Group has an Excellent Change Success Score, the Cloud Infrastructure change model has > 90% success, the change has no conflicts, the change will be auto approved.
<CLICK> For this type of change, Implementation will occur automatically during the scheduled timeframe via automated tools / templates.
Once the mandatory fields have been completed, the change will auto transition to Closed state and the outcome will logged by the associated Flow.

ServiceNow AIOps is different than IT point solutions. It is at once more robust, more integrated, and more automated.
Like certain point solutions on the market it ingests events, logs, and metrics including those from the various applications, monitoring and observability tools you already use.
Like certain separate point solutions, ServiceNow AI and ML can use highly refined and diverse techniques to correlate and deduplicate ALERTS, eliminating up to 98% of the noise and surfacing only the few actionable alerts that need your attention.
Only ServiceNow AIOps bring those functions together on your service and operations platform to allow you to automatically respond to those alerts with predefined workflows and resolution playbooks. It can resolve some issues without human intervention although the automated remediation can also be coordinated with human support teams using standard collaboration tools.
We use several correlation and anomaly detection techniques to understand the data ingested from your monitoring tools :
We use Tag-based Alert Clustering – this technique lets you get started right away with AIOps even without a fully populated CMDB. Tag-based Alert Clustering applies machine learning techniques to the content of tags to identify patterns. Furthermore, it normalizes tags to better organize alerts.
We use Automated Temporal Analysis – a technique that runs a nightly job to evaluate a 30-day rolling window and identify patterns. It uses a simple feedback mechanism so you can help the ML understand if its alert clustering tactic is on-track. With each iteration of feedback the ML gets smarter and better able to spot and predict real issues.
We use Topological analysis – where you can use the topology from Basic Discovery or Service Maps to identify issues like bottlenecks, single points of failure, and areas with high traffic and resource utilization.
We apply the clustering and analysis methos to logs, events, and alerts.
Our AI first uses logs to learn your environment . (Note that our AI does not have to be told where to look for in advance, nor do you have to set thresholds or create patterns as you would have to do for other AI point solutions.)
Our AI continues to evaluate logs and having seen enough cause for concern it will raise an alert (The concerning data may come in the form of metrics in recent logs that reach a preset thresholds or unexpected events that fit a pattern) .
The AI then goes to work on events and alerts
The AI can correlate related events and group them into actionable alerts.
To fix the problem, you can collaborate with support teams and leverage more than 175 integrations from Automation Engine to automatically remediate the issue using workflows.
Every element of ServiceNow Predictive AIOps is designed to help you quicky resolve alerts well before they become incidents - The result for your business is - improved service availability, customer satisfaction and business agility to keep your digital business running 24/7.

As organizations adopt new tools and workloads, they face tool sprawl and data silos that fragment service visibility. Extensible Data Integration: Supports data ingestion from cloud providers, ServiceNow agents, and third-party tools (e.g., APM solutions, Kubernetes), providing a full-stack view of service health.

Summary
Now Assist for CMDB introduces AI-driven enhancements that streamline Configuration Item (CI) management, reduce duplicate data, and improve decision-making by summarizing and interpreting complex CMDB data. Leveraging the power of ServiceNow’s AI and Natural Language Query (NLQ) capabilities, this update empowers IT teams to address CI remediation at scale, improve CMDB health, and automate tedious de-duplication tasks.
Chargeable
Now Assist for ConCMDB is automatically available to anyone with Technology Workflow Professional Plus SKU. It still requires installation of the skills and consumes assists purchased as part of any other SKU (including non-Technology SKUs like Now Assist for HR).
Challenge
Modern CMDBs contain vast amounts of data spread across multiple tables, making it difficult for teams to quickly understand the state of a CI and its impact on services. Duplicate CIs not only degrade the health of the CMDB but also lead to operational inefficiencies, resulting in longer resolution times. Teams also face challenges in extracting actionable insights from their CMDB data without navigating through complex data models.
Business Need:
For IT operations to run smoothly, businesses need a healthy CMDB that accurately reflects their infrastructure. Duplicate CIs, inconsistent data, and a lack of visibility into relationships between CIs undermine the CMDB’s effectiveness. Organizations require a tool that can simplify CI management, eliminate duplicate data, and provide real-time insights into the health and state of their tech assets.
Solution
Now Assist for CMDB provides several key features to address these challenges:
AI-Powered Summarization: Using Now Assist’s conversational interface, users can ask for CI summaries, helping them quickly understand the state of any CI without needing to navigate multiple tables. This reduces the number of steps needed to access critical information.
De-Duplication at Scale: Now Assist leverages de-duplication template APIs to analyze and resolve duplicate CIs at scale. The conversational workflow helps users prioritize and remediate duplicates quickly, ensuring that the CMDB maintains high data quality.
Conversational Insights: By using NLQ and Virtual Agent frameworks, Now Assist allows users to ask complex CMDB questions in natural language and receive actionable insights without needing a deep understanding of the underlying data model. This reduces friction and speeds up decision-making.

Summary:
Now Assist for Service Graph Connectors (SGC) brings AI-powered diagnostics and troubleshooting to Service Graph connector issues, helping IT teams resolve errors faster and reduce downtime. By summarizing errors and leveraging ServiceNow’s AI capabilities, users can automatically retrieve relevant knowledge base (KB) articles and suggested solutions, improving productivity and minimizing manual troubleshooting.
Chargeable
Now Assist for Service Graph Connectors (SGC) is automatically available to anyone with Technology Workflow Professional Plus SKU. It still requires installation of the skills and consumes assists purchased as part of any other SKU (including non-Technology SKUs like Now Assist for HR).
Challenge:
Diagnosing and debugging Service Graph connector issues can be time-consuming and complex, often requiring manual investigation to pinpoint the cause. Misconfigurations or data import failures can disrupt business operations, and without clear, actionable insights, support teams struggle to quickly resolve the root cause.
Business Need:
Organizations need a tool that can simplify the identification and resolution of Service Graph connector errors. Reducing mean time to resolution (MTTR) for support cases is critical for maintaining operational continuity, especially when integrating various systems through certified connectors. Automating error diagnosis and providing immediate recommendations helps teams focus on higher-value tasks rather than manual troubleshooting.
Solution:
Now Assist for SGC enhances the diagnostic process with several key features:
AI-Driven Error Summaries: Now Assist summarizes complex error logs into human-readable explanations, helping users quickly understand what went wrong and why.
KB Article Recommendations: After summarizing the issue, Now Assist automatically searches for relevant knowledge base articles and suggests actionable solutions, reducing the need for manual investigation.
Conversational Assistance: Through a conversational interface, users can directly ask Now Assist to diagnose connector issues. It will analyze the problem, summarize the error, and provide step-by-step recommendations for resolution.

slides.title: Employee asset receiving
slides.text:
Employee asset receiving
Hardware Asset Management (HAM)
> Capabilities
> HAM
Improved efficiency and accuracy for employees receiving assets
Prompt employees to receive assets in transit from Employee Center notifications
Automatically update any related PO, shipment, or asset task after an employee receives an asset
Increase data accuracy with real-time updates to asset records upon receipt
1
2
3
Summary​​
Asset managers want employees to receive assets from the Employee Center for accountability and tracking purposes. End-users can lose productivity with a clunky receiving process. Decreased data accuracy also occurs when real-time updates for asset receiving are not given or available. Employee asset receiving feature prompts employees to receive assets in transit from Employee Center notifications. It automatically updates any related PO, TO, shipment, or asset task after the employee receives an asset, increasing data accuracy with real-time updates to asset receiving. This feature ensures that assets are properly managed and accounted for, enhancing overall operational efficiency.
Chargeable​​
Included with Hardware Asset Management Professional
Challenge​​
Manual nature of receiving assets can lead to gaps between the shipping and inventory stages, which often results in lost or misplaced assets
Lack of structured workflow can also cause inefficiencies and errors in updating asset records
Business Need​​
Improved efficiency for asset receipt and reduce time and effort required
Mitigate the risk of losing or misplacing assets and improve inventory accuracy
​​
Solution​​
Employee asset receiving improves accuracy for receiving assets. This feature prompts employees to receive assets in transit from Employee Center notifications and automatically updates any related purchase orders (PO), transfer orders (TO), shipments, or asset tasks after the employee receives an asset. It also increases data accuracy with real-time updates to asset receiving.
Target Persona(s) ​
Asset Managers, warehouse personnel, technical staff

Summary​​
Hardware asset managers often deal with a large volume of hardware asset requests that can quickly turn into a backlog of mundane fulfillment requests. Clearing this backlog can be time-consuming and whittle down HAM managers’ valuable time that could be spent on higher value activities instead. Help manage asset requests brings AI agents to help asset managers fulfill hardware requests more efficiently. This workflow improves the overall experience in managing large volumes of hardware requests and accelerates the request fulfillment time thanks to AI agents assisting the fulfillers. This improves productivity and enables HAM managers to focus more on high-value activities.
Chargeable​​
Included with Hardware Asset Management Professional Plus
Challenge​​
Users spend significant time with manual tasks when sourcing asset requests, often at the expense of efficiency and employee experience
High volumes of asset requests result in high-lead times for hardware and delays in request fulfillment due to clogged sourcing requests in queues
Time-consuming and repetitive manual tasks to consume, create transfer orders and purchase orders
Business Need​​
Remove manual tasks from asset managers’ queues with AI agents making autonomous, nondeterministic decisions
HAM managers can allocate valuable time to higher value activities and avoid getting bogged down by administrative tasks
Improve employee experience with faster access to assets
​​
Solution​​
Help manage asset requests improves the employee experience with AI agents to fulfill hardware asset requests. This workflow improves the hardware request process, accelerates request fulfillment times, and optimizes workflows for increased productivity.

HAM manger, HAM user

Chat Wrap-Up & Summarize:

Upon concluding a chat, an agent can trigger a summary by clicking the Summarize button
A purple banner appears below the Details (tab label) displaying a GenAI summary

Case Wrap-Up & Summarize:
Summarize work notes and set resolution code powered by GenAI
Upon closing a case, an agent can trigger a summary by clicking the Summarize button
Now Assist for Workspace
A conversational panel appearing within CSM Configurable Workspace whereby agents an trigger GAI actions, such as, Case Summarization or draft a knowledge article
Challenge
To solve a customer issue agents are often required to read and interpret information from many parts of the Case record, spanning time, with input from many possible persons. This can be a tedious and time consuming task, especially for complex multi-touch cases.
Previously, agents and managers would be required to read the entire chat transcript to understand a customer’s issue. Manually reading a chat transcript is time consuming and may lead to inconsistent summaries across agents
When a common problem arises support teams need to rapidly create and share solutions
Support teams seek to provide timely and accurate response to customer inquires
Business Need
Save time – By rapidly gaining contextual understanding of the customer's issue
Reduce resolution time
Improve operational accuracy and insight
Enable agents and managers to make decisions quicker
Solution
With cases, leveraging GenAI we are instantly creating a summary of the work notes. This summary reflects the complete life-cycle of the case, including back-and-forward dialog via portal comments
With chats, This summary reflects the complete life-cycle of the interaction. That is from the customer’s interaction with VA, to a live agent, and/or agent-to-agent chats
Leveraging GAI, agents can trigger requests from with the Workspace

With ServiceNow's Workplace Service Delivery we’ve created a solution that helps you craft a modern workplace.
It all starts with the employee experience. No more wrestling with office logistics. Whether you're in an office, lab, or even a courthouse- across Teams, Outlook, mobile, or the ServiceNow portal - scheduling your space, booking rooms, picking a desk, or requesting services is streamlined and intuitive. Employees dive into their work instead of getting tangled up in workplace coordination.
And you can’t have a great employee experience without knowing what's happening in your buildings. Which floors are busy? Which rooms sit empty? Instead of spreadsheets and guesswork, you get clear data about how people actually use your space, so you can make it work better for everyone.
And we help your workplace run smoothly. Instead of rushing to fix things when they break, get ahead of problems. Track work orders, schedule maintenance before things break down, and give your facilities team the tools they need to keep everything running smoothly. From fixing broken coffee machines to managing building systems - when operations run better, people can focus on their work instead of dealing with workplace headaches.
This modern workplace leads to increased in-office employee satisfaction, better utilization of spaces, and reduction in asset repair & maintenance.

AI Platform
These are the 8 core competencies of operational resilience—each one unlocks a critical capability your bank needs to survive and thrive in today's environment.
1: Continuous Service & Enterprise Asset Mapping
—The master key. AI maintains real-time visibility of every asset and dependency. You can't protect what you can't see.
2: Autonomous IT Operations—Transform your tech from reactive to autonomous. AI self-heals infrastructure before customers even notice issues.
3: Risk & Compliance—Turn regulatory changes into automated action. AI translates DORA, Basel IV requirements directly into control updates.
4: Security AND Operational Vulnerabilities—Two distinct threats. For security: when CISA announces critical CVEs, AI instantly surfaces affected assets with automated patching. For operational: AI continuously monitors high-risk processes—wire transfer limits, segregation of duties, mandatory leave—catching control breaches before auditors do.
5: Business Continuity—Move beyond annual tests. AI continuously validates your ability to stay within impact tolerances under real-world scenarios.
6: Incident Response—When crisis hits, AI orchestrates recovery by business priority while humans are still reading alerts.
7: Third-Party Management—Your vendors' risks are your risks. AI monitors certifications, tests patches, and predicts cascade failures across your ecosystem.
8: AI Governance & Reporting—Control your AI while it controls your operations. Real-time resilience KPIs with explainable AI decisions, complete audit trails, and embedded attestation workflows. Transform board conversations from 'what went wrong' to 'what's our AI predicting next.'
Each competency is essential— but the power isn't in any single competency—it's in breaking down the silos between them. When your risk, security, IT ops, and business continuity systems share one intelligence layer, threats discovered in one area trigger defenses everywhere. That's true operational resilience—not eight separate programs, but one unified defense.

Increasing threats across cyber attacks, rapid cloud migration and hybrid clouds, increasing numbers of third-party risks, data protection and privacy concerns, the growing number and evolving regulations, is forcing risk managers to reconsider their investments in technology.
In 2021, global banks incurred $20.3 billion in operational loss (which could stem from fraud, regulatory fines, risk posed by third parties, or the exploitation of unmitigated risk). To address this worrisome statistic, top investment areas for Risk Managers this year include: data analytics, process automation, detection and monitoring risks, integrated risk management, and workflow management.
Some of the greatest challenges are created by the regulatory environment. And the number of regulations have grown significantly in recent years directly relating to IT, Cyber and broader Operational Resilience. The Bank of England’s Op Res Regulation, DORA EU Legislation, Bafin Section 44 in Germany and APRA C… are all examples of an increasingly tight regulatory environment, and migration to hyper scaler clouds to support infrastructure resilience, cost and growth opportunities brings with it additional challenges in regulation. Sadly, many banks have historically underinvested in compliance or security and technology risk management systems and tools, leading to ineffective controls, processes, and analysis.
Ever-increasing security threats and evolving regulatory requirements are putting a strain on the inadequate solutions currently in place - forcing change for banks' risk and compliance management processes.

Enterprise Asset Management is the process of overseeing the full lifecycle of an organization’s physical business assets to meet operational targets, maximize usable life, and minimize risk. Starting with planning the business asset needs to acquiring equipment to deploying items and managing enterprise assets during operations and maintenance, and ultimately retiring them. Throughout the lifecycle, ask yourself these three questions:
What enterprise business assets do you own?​ Many companies we talk to simply want to get a better handle on the connected and non-connected things they own or lease and where the are at any given point in time.
Can you streamline enterprise asset processes? We can help you automate away the paper, spreadsheets, and all the in-between steps.
Are you maximizing useable asset life and mitigating risk? Maybe you have a bunch of unused assets sitting on the shelf that could be redistributed or you are constantly running out of certain stockroom items.
EAM helps answer these types of questions so you can track an enterprise asset through its entire lifecycle, which is all made easier with a single source of a truth on the ServiceNow AI Platform.”

App Engine’s native governance—App Engine Management Center—empowers teams with the tools they need to scale their low-code development. Developers can submit app ideas, invite others to build together, and hand them off to IT for tests and deployments—all in a streamlined workspace environment. IT can establish guardrails within the development environment for effective governance and enterprise-class support. By leveraging built-in collaboration tools, app templates, and role-based access, you can expand your developer pool while ensuring application security and best practices.
App Engine’s governance tools simply give you more control without adding to your workload, meaning you can confidently bust your backlog knowing any collaborator—from IT to LOB—is set up for success.

The ServiceNow colocation facilities and cloud-based infrastructure, are designed to be highly available with redundant components and multiple network paths to avoid single points of failure. This Advanced High Availability architecture provides the primary means to restore service in the case of a disruption that could impact availability.
The Recovery Point Objective is one hour, and the Recovery Time Objective is two hours.
The ServiceNow colocation facilities are arranged in pairs, with all customer production data hosted in both colocation facilities. These pairs are kept in sync using asynchronous database replication.
Both colocation facilities are always operational, with data replicated from the active read‐write colocation facility to the passive read‐only colocation facility.
Data at rest is stored in a contractually defined colocation facility region.
Prior to executing maintenance, ServiceNow can proactively transfer operation of a customer instance from one colocation facility to the other. The maintenance can then proceed without impacting service availability. Therefore, transfer between active and passive colocation facilities is regularly executed as part of ServiceNow standard operating procedures.
This practice ensures that if a failover is needed, the transfer will be successful with minimal service disruption.

slides.text:

In certain scenarios, it may be necessary to use traditional backup and recovery mechanisms. For example, if a customer's data is accidentally deleted or corrupted, rendering it unusable or inaccessible. In this case, restoring from a backup is the only option for recovery.
Full backups are taken weekly, with differential backups performed every 24 hours.
All backups are written to disk; tapes and removable media are not used.
Backups are not sent off‐site and remain in the colocation facility where they are made, which provides geographic separation.
At the end of their working life, disks are securely wiped, or destroyed, so that no data remains.
Backups are encrypted with AES-256 using randomly generated encryption keys for every backup.
Keys are kept in a secure key store, and only retrieved by an automated process.
ServiceNow runs regular, automated tests to ensure the quality of backups, and any failures are reported for remediation. The ServiceNow backup architecture is not designed to provide archival records, given the 14-day backup retention period.
However, customers may choose to retain data within their instances for as long as they require, in accordance with their policy or regulatory requirements.

slides.title: LDAP Integration
slides.text:
LDAP integration allows your instance to use your existing LDAP server as the primary source of user data.
Administrators integrate with a Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) directory to streamline the user login process and to automate administrative tasks such as creating users and assigning them roles. An LDAP integration allows the system to use your existing LDAP server as the primary source of user data. Typically, an LDAP integration is also part of a single sign-on implementation.
The integration uses the LDAP service account credentials to retrieve the user distinguished name (DN) from the LDAP server. Given the DN value for the user, the integration then rebinds with LDAP with the user's DN and password. The password that the user enters is contained entirely in the HTTPS session.

ServiceNow Zero Trust Access is a security tool for security administrators to reduce the privileges available to a user in a session based on various risk parameters. They can create contextual policies to define the level of access a user should get based on network, location, authentication method and identity provider attributes.
Zero-Trust Access offers a significant improvement in cybersecurity and data protection compared to traditional security models because it assumes no trust by default, meaning that every user, device, or application trying to access a company's resources must be verified and authorized before gaining access. ServiceNow’s Zero Trust Access delivers several key benefits:
Granular access control: Zero-Trust Access allows organizations to implement fine-grained access controls based on contextual policies (user identity, location, network, etc..). This enables customers to enforce the principle of least privilege, granting users only the necessary access required to perform their specific tasks.
Improved security posture: Zero-Trust Access minimizes the attack surface by constantly verifying the identity and trustworthiness of users and devices attempting to access sensitive data or applications. This significantly reduces the risk of unauthorized access, data breaches, and other cyber threats.
Protect against insider threats: Traditional security models assume trust for users within the network, which can lead to vulnerabilities from insider threats or compromised credentials. Zero-Trust Access mitigates these risks by consistently verifying the identity and access privileges of all users, regardless of their location or affiliation.
Improved compliance: Many industries have stringent regulatory requirements concerning data privacy and security. Implementing Zero-Trust Access can help organizations meet these compliance standards by ensuring secure access and data protection.
ServiceNow Zero-Trust Access offers customers a proactive and robust security approach that bolsters cybersecurity defenses and ensures a safer environment for their critical assets including users, devices and applications.

slides.title: Top Pricing & Packaging FAQs
slides.text:
Top Pricing & Packaging FAQs
Question
Do customers have to pay for an Azure OpenAI license to be able to use Now Assist features?
No, customers do not need to purchase a separate license to be able to use the Now Assist features included in the Pro Plus, Enterprise Plus, and Creator Pro Plus SKUs.
Are assists pooled? At what level?
Yes. Assists are pooled across all instances on a customer’s account. That means they are shared between license holders, and between products.
What is the difference between Creator Pro Plus and App Engine Enterprise Plus?
Creator Pro Plus includes build time skills that make it easier to create objects on the Platform; App Engine Pro Plus includes runtime features that enable customers to inject AI into custom workflows.
How will customers know how many assists they have used?
As of December 2023, customers on Vancouver or later are able to view assist usage in Subscription Management for an individual instance; aggregate usage will be available in June (estimate; subject to change)
Is Now Assist available in restricted environments?
Yes. Beginning June 28, 2024, Now Assist SKUs are generally available in the Government Community Cloud and Singapore Hybrid (RM Level 2) and are offered on a restricted basis for self-hosted customers. Note that GCC and self-hosted require different SKUs vs. commercial environments.
Can customers still use the Controller to build their own use cases?
Yes, customers purchasing Pro/Enterprise/Creator Pro Plus SKUs can connect custom apps to external LLM accounts using the Controller. External LLM calls using the Controller consume one assist per call.

Speaker Notes:
Let’s talk about what CSDM actually is—and what it isn’t.
Many customers hear "CSDM" and assume it’s an extra layer of work. But the truth is, you don’t do CSDM separately. You benefit from it by simply using the platform the way it’s designed—building services, applications, and teams into a single, consistent structure.
What you see here is that structure—CSDM v5. It moves from left to right, following the natural lifecycle of a digital product or service—from initial idea to how it’s consumed by users and customers.
We start on the left with Ideation & Strategy. This is where business goals are captured early—things like new product ideas, strategic initiatives, or capability gaps.
Next comes Design & Planning. Here, the teams define what they’re building—whether that’s an app, a service, or an offering. CSDM helps bridge business and IT by tying that plan to things like demand records, service portfolios, and product catalogs.
In Build & Integration, the design becomes reality. Components are developed, integrations are defined, and CI relationships start forming—many of which are discovered automatically.
Then we move into Service Delivery. This is where services run in production, tied to real application services and infrastructure. With CSDM, those are modeled in a way that reflects how the business actually consumes and experiences them.
Finally, there’s Service Consumption. CSDM lets you track not just what’s running, but how it’s being used—by whom, in what business context, and with what impact. That makes it easier to manage outcomes, adoption, and alignment to value streams.
The beauty of this model is that it’s already present in the ServiceNow platform. Each part gets built as teams do their work—developing, deploying, delivering. The value of CSDM is that it connects those pieces into one cohesive structure, without adding extra effort.
And because it’s consistent across the platform, everything else works better: workflows, policies, dashboards, AI agents. They’re all more effective because the model behind them is solid.
On the next slide, we’ll look at a real example of how this plays out for something every business has—a sales capability—and how easy it is to map using this approach.

This slide illustrates the strength of our data model, which is out-of-the-box, highly reusable, and ready to support all business processes.At the bottom, we see the foundation data, the basic building blocks such as company, users, departments, workgroups, contracts, and partners. These are the foundations on which everything else relies.In the middle, we find the Task table, from which all other work units derive, such as incident, case, change, problem, request. This means that every type of operational activity a company manages can be modeled and tracked in the same way, ensuring consistency and simplicity.On the right, we see the Configuration Item table, which is the root of all CMDB classes. From here derive databases, servers, applications, services, and even OT assets. In other words, everything that makes up your infrastructure and services is already represented in a coherent data model.Another key aspect is that this model already includes predefined relationships across tables. This enables easy and powerful data navigation, what we call dot walking. Task Mining
ServiceNow AI Platform
Analyze workstation task execution for end-to-end process improvement

Summary​​
Part of Process Mining, Task mining is a systematic, data-focused approach that captures and analyzes user interactions with digital systems and applications (even outside of the ServiceNow platform), seeking to reveal how manual tasks are executed within business processes.
Chargeable​​
Store application. After installation, the customer will have access to the Task Mining Workspace and up to 40 application users, bundled with 125,000 records for Process Mining.
Challenge​​
Processes are rarely linear and often span multiple systems managed by different business units.
Variations in these processes can result from poor design, as well as from the way people perform tasks.
To gain a proper understanding of how work is carried out at the workstation level, Task Mining is essential.
Business Need​
Access to the complex user data and insights to enable informed decision-making.
Move beyond guesswork and biased anecdotes often shared by those immersed in routine tasks.
Deliver deep insights, advanced analytics, and a solid foundation for automation initiatives.
​​
Solution​​
It is ideal to start with Task Mining to:
Provide visibility into how manual work is performed.
Explore opportunities for automation.
Inspect inefficiencies or variations in processes but can’t pinpoint the root causes.
Prepare for digital transformation, M&A, or scaling operations.
Complement Process Mining analysis with user interaction data.

Continuous Improvement Managers and Process Owners – to perform deep process analysis
Automation CoE Owners – to quantify ROI of automation ideas
IT & Ops Leaders – to understand IT landscape and app usage

An update set is a group of configuration changes that can be moved from one instance to another.
The installation procedure should include instructions for:
Update set order
Additional data or configuration changes required to accompany the update sets
Activating plugins
Configuring system properties or other instance-specific settings
Setting up MID Servers and identity servers
Ensuring that the target table is available

Update Sets
Storing changes to a base system or installed application.Storing and applying a particular version of an application.
Producing a file for export.
You can manually create update sets to store a particular application version. Use update sets to deploy patches or changes to installed applications.
Note: Don’t use update sets to install applications. Instead, use the application repository or the ServiceNow Store to install applications.
Application Repository
Installing and updating applications on all company instances. Automatically managing application update sets.
Restricting access to applications to the same company.
Deploying completed applications to end users.
Consider uploading an application to the ServiceNow Store to share it with other users.
